ExpandBlogPostFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=markup` to include the PML markup for the post's visual content. Markup is opt-in on every endpoint (show, list, create, update) because PML serialization runs per post. See the [Expanding guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/expand) for available fields and examples.
ExpandBlogPostFields.name: expand[]

ExpandCodeFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=field_name` to include optional fields (e.g., `expand[]=head_code&expand[]=footer_code`). See the [Expanding guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/expand) for available fields and examples.
ExpandCodeFields.name: expand[]

ExpandContactFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=field_name` to include optional fields (e.g., `expand[]=email_engagement`). See the [Expanding guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/expand) for available fields and examples.
ExpandContactFields.name: expand[]

ExpandEmailsBroadcastStatsFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=variants` to include a `variants` array with each split-test variant's numbers, split into the test and the winner's send.
ExpandEmailsBroadcastStatsFields.name: expand[]

ExpandFunnelFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=field_name` to include optional fields. Available fields: head_code, footer_code. See the [Expanding guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/expand) for examples.
ExpandFunnelFields.name: expand[]

ExpandFunnelStatsFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=steps` to include per-step statistics. When `expand[]=steps` is set, the response contains a `steps` array with detailed metrics for each funnel step. When omitted, the response contains a `page_public_ids` array instead. See [the expanded steps response](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/stats/skill.md#response-with-expandsteps) in the [Stats Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/stats/skill.md) for both response shapes.
ExpandFunnelStatsFields.name: expand[]

ExpandPageFields.description: Expand additional data in the response. Use `expand[]=field_name` to include optional fields (e.g., `expand[]=head_code&expand[]=footer_code&expand[]=custom_css&expand[]=markup`). Markup is opt-in on every endpoint (show, list, create, update) because PML serialization runs per page. `custom_css` is available on internal pages only. See the [Expanding guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/expand) for available fields and examples. Read a page's existing markup with `expand[]=markup` before editing it: see [Reading Current Markup](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#reading-current-markup) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md).
ExpandPageFields.name: expand[]

InvoiceFilter.name: filter

external_id.description: A comma-separated list of External IDs to filter by.

id.description: A comma-separated list of Invoice IDs to filter by.

invoice_number.description: A comma-separated list of Invoice Numbers to filter by.

invoice_type.description: The type of the invoice to filter by.

status.description: The status of the invoice to filter by.

StatsTimerangeEnd.description: End of the stats timerange (ISO 8601 only; any other value is a 422. Send an offset's `+` as `%2B`, since an unencoded `+` arrives as a space). Defaults to the current time. Values in the future are automatically clamped to now.

AccountSuspended.description:
Forbidden — the account behind this request has been suspended by ClickFunnels: the user or
team the access token acts for, or the team the request acts on. Every endpoint refuses a
suspended account, reads included, and the body carries `"code": "account_suspended"`.

example.error: Service unavailable: This request ran out of its 20s budget before the filter could be evaluated, so no records were read. The filter itself was not found to be too broad, so retrying is worth doing.

FilteredQueryBudget.description:
Service Unavailable — retryable. Two conditions land here:

* **Transient dependency** — a database connection, the model behind filter generation, or another
  dependency was briefly unavailable.
* **Request budget exhausted** — the request's own wall clock ran out before the filter could be given a
  fair slice, so no records were read. The time went elsewhere in the same request: a slow generation
  call, or earlier pages of the same projection.

The second case is the OPPOSITE of the 422 that says the filter "took longer than 10s to evaluate". That
422 is a statement timeout and is deterministic — the filter selects more than can be evaluated, and an
unchanged retry fails identically. This 503 makes no such claim about the filter, so retrying is worth
doing; if it recurs, narrow the filter or ask for fewer records per call.

WorkspaceGrantForbidden.description:
Forbidden — this request's workspace is closed to it.

Four cases return this:

* The access token is limited to specific workspaces (see the workspace selection made when
  the key was provisioned, or the workspaces approved on the OAuth consent screen) and the
  request acts on a workspace outside that set.
* The access token is limited to specific workspaces and the request's workspace could not be
  determined at all. The gate is fail-closed, so a workspace-limited token is denied rather
  than allowed through when the target workspace is ambiguous.
* The workspace's team has no active ClickFunnels subscription: it was canceled, is paused,
  or is locked out after failed payments. Reads and writes are both refused until the
  subscription is reactivated, and the body carries `"code": "subscription_inactive"`.
* The account behind the request has been suspended by ClickFunnels: the user or team the
  access token acts for, or the workspace or team the request acts on. Reads and writes are
  both refused, and the body carries `"code": "account_suspended"`.

A token with no workspace restriction never receives the first two.

ConditionalSplitStepAttributes.description:
A conditional split step routes contacts down one of two branches based on whether
they match a contact filter (`condition`). Each branch carries the
`show_page_step` + `page` attached to that branch (both `null` when the branch is
empty). The first branch (`branches[0]`) is the **matched** branch; the second
(`branches[1]`) is the **unmatched** branch.

See the [Funnels Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#conditional-split-steps) for the full conditional-split surface (positioning, multi-page branches, attaching filters).

The `condition.filter_id` is the public id of a RefineFilter scoped to the same workspace.
Pass it on PATCH to attach or replace the filter. Create filters first via `POST /api/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}/refine_filters` — see [Attaching a filter](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#attaching-a-filter) and the cross-link to [Applying filters to conditional split steps](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#applying-filters-to-conditional-split-steps).

On `GET /funnels/{funnel_id}/conditional_split_steps/{id}` (show), `condition.filter` is always
included as a full RefineFilter object. On the list endpoint it is included only when
`expand[]=filter` is passed.

page.description: The page attached to this branch, or null if empty.

show_page_step.description: The ShowPageStep function attached to this branch, or null if empty.

filter.description:
The full RefineFilter object for the attached filter. Always present on the show endpoint.
Present on the list endpoint only when `expand[]=filter` is requested. Absent (key omitted)
when no filter is attached or the expand param is not passed.

filter_id.description: Public id of the attached RefineFilter. `null` when no filter has been set up.

is_setup.description: True when a filter has been attached and the conditional split is ready to evaluate.

funnel_id.description: ID of the funnel containing this conditional split

ConditionalSplitStepAttributes.title: Conditional Split Step

ConditionalSplitStepParametersCreate.description:
Parameters for adding a new conditional split step to a funnel's workflow. The split
always starts as a 2-branch tree (`matched` first, `unmatched` second). All fields
below are optional — providing none creates an empty unconfigured split that
the caller can fill in later via PATCH.

### `condition`

Supply `filter_id` — the public id of a RefineFilter scoped to the same workspace.
Create filters first via `POST /api/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}/refine_filters`.
Raw numeric ids are rejected for cross-tenant safety. See [Attaching a filter](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#attaching-a-filter)
and [Applying filters to conditional split steps](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#applying-filters-to-conditional-split-steps).

### Branches

Optional `branches` array — up to 2 entries; `branches[0]` is the matched branch,
`branches[1]` is the unmatched branch. Each entry may carry either:

- `page_id` — a single fresh `user_page` id to attach as the branch's first step.
- `page_ids` — an array of fresh `user_page` ids to attach in order. Use this to
  build a branch with multiple sequential pages (e.g. matched users see Welcome →
  Onboarding → CTA, while unmatched users see Email Capture → Welcome).

`page_id` and `page_ids` are mutually exclusive per branch entry. Each page
referenced must be in the same workspace and not already wired to any
`ShowPageStep` anywhere.

### Positioning

See `show_page_step_id` semantics — identical to the split test step endpoint.

branches.description: Optional 0..2 branch entries; `branches[0]` is the matched branch, `branches[1]` is the unmatched branch.

page_id.description: Optional id of a page with no existing show-page step (an unattached internal page or a standalone external page) to attach as the branch's first step. Mutually exclusive with `page_ids`. See [Placing an external (SDK) page in a branch](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#placing-an-external-sdk-page-in-a-branch) in the [Funnels Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md) for creating the standalone external page you reference here.

page_ids.description:
Optional list of fresh `user_page` ids to attach in order under this branch.
Use this to build branches with multiple sequential steps. Mutually exclusive with `page_id`.

filter_id.description: Public id of a RefineFilter in this workspace. Create filters via `POST /api/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}/refine_filters`.

show_page_step_id.description:
Optional. Insert the new conditional split AFTER the workflow step that wraps
this `show_page_step`. Accepts a numeric `Workflows::Steps::ShowPageStep` id
or its obfuscated public id (you can read either off any page response).
When omitted, the split lands at funnel entry.
Caution: creating a split moves the wrapped step inside a branch sequence,
so an id fetched earlier may no longer sit where you think — read the
funnel structure immediately before creating, and note that anchoring on
a step inside another split's branch nests the new split in that branch.

ConditionalSplitStepParametersUpdate.description:
Update the `condition` and/or attach pages to existing `branches`. At least one of
the two must be provided.

- `condition.filter_id` is the public id of a RefineFilter in the same workspace.
  Create or update filters via the RefineFilter endpoints. See [Attaching a filter](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#attaching-a-filter)
  and [Applying filters to conditional split steps](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#applying-filters-to-conditional-split-steps).
- `branches` must be a 2-entry array (matched, unmatched).
  - `page_id` (single) — when the branch is empty: attach. When the branch already
    has show-page-steps: swap the FIRST step's page (subsequent steps preserved).
  - `page_ids` (array) — APPEND the listed fresh pages to the end of the branch.
    Use this to grow a branch with more sequential steps over multiple PATCHes.
  Both forms are mutually exclusive per entry; any page referenced must be a
  fresh `user_page` in the same workspace with no existing ShowPageStep.

page_ids.description: List of fresh page ids to APPEND to the end of this branch. Mutually exclusive with `page_id`.

custom_attributes.description:
Custom attributes are usually added in ClickFunnels to a contact when they submit forms that contain custom contact attributes. Here you can directly create them during contact modification.

Custom attributes are provided as key-value pairs:
A key that does not exist, will create a new custom contact attribute.
A key that already exists, will update the value of an existing custom contact attribute.

Empty or null values, will set the custom attribute values to empty strings. A key that has special characters or spaces will be automatically converted to `snake_case` (For example, 'Favorite Food! 🥑' will be converted to 'favorite_food').

Empty keys will trigger a bad request response. Also, non-object inputs for custom_attributes (e.g. an array or string), it will be ignored.
Keys that are default properties on the Contact resource or variations of it will result in an error. E.g., 'first_name', 'First Name',  etc. are not valid inputs.

CoursesSectionsPublishActionAttributes.description: Asynchronous action that publishes one or more course sections and their lessons

approved_by_id.description: ID of the membership that approved this action (reserved for future use).

auto_enroll.description: When `true`, existing course enrollees are automatically granted access to the newly published sections.

completed_at.description: Datetime the async job finished. `null` until complete.

course_id.description: ID of the course whose sections are being published

created_by_id.description: ID of the workspace membership that created this action.

offer_new_section_via_all_access_product.description: When `true`, products that grant full course access are updated to also offer the newly published sections.

performed_count.description: Number of sections processed so far. Poll alongside `target_count` to track async progress.

published_lessons_count.description: Number of lesson publish timestamps this action changed. Immediate actions make those lessons live, including individually scheduled lessons they force-publish; a future one-step course launch assigns its requested future timestamp instead. Lessons already live are excluded. The one-step count is recorded synchronously per section, so it reflects that flow's work rather than `0`.

scheduled_for.description: When set, the action is deferred until this datetime. Must be a future datetime. `null` means execute immediately.

send_email.description: When `true` (and `auto_enroll` is also `true`), enrolled contacts receive an email notification about the newly published sections.

started_at.description: Datetime the async job began processing sections. `null` until started.

status.description: Progress of the async receipt: `queued` (saved, not yet started), `scheduled` (deferred to a future `scheduled_for`), `processing` (running), or `completed`. Poll this to tell whether work is still ongoing without inferring it from the timestamps.

target_all.description: When `true`, every unpublished non-root section of the course is targeted for publishing. Mutually exclusive with `target_ids`.

target_count.description: Total number of sections targeted by this action. `null` until the async job has resolved the count.

target_ids.description: Explicit list of course-section IDs targeted for publishing, always emitted as integers. The create request also accepts public IDs, which are resolved on input. Mutually exclusive with `target_all`.

CoursesSectionsPublishActionAttributes.title: Course Section Publish Actions

CoursesSectionsPublishActionParameters.description: Parameters for creating a course-section publish action. Select exactly one of a nonempty `target_ids` array or `target_all: true`.

auto_enroll.description: When `true`, existing course enrollees are granted access to the newly published sections automatically.

offer_new_section_via_all_access_product.description: When `true`, products that grant full course access are updated to also include the newly published sections.

scheduled_for.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime. The publish is deferred until this time. Must be a future datetime. Omit to publish immediately.

send_email.description: When `true` (requires `auto_enroll: true`), enrolled contacts receive an email notification about the newly published sections.

target_all.description: Set to `true` to publish every unpublished non-root section of the course. Mutually exclusive with `target_ids`. Exactly one of `target_all` or `target_ids` must be supplied.

target_ids.description: Array of course-section public IDs to publish. Mutually exclusive with `target_all`. Exactly one of `target_ids` or `target_all` must be supplied.

DiscountAttributes.description: A reusable, workspace-scoped discount applied on top of a price.

active.description: Derived - true when the discount is neither scheduled for the future nor expired.

amount.description: Fixed amount off, as a decimal string (e.g. "10.00"). `null` for a percentage discount.

applies_to.description: Scope of the discount. `all_products` (the default) applies workspace-wide; the `specific_*` values restrict it to the ids passed in `product_ids` / `variant_ids` / `products_collection_ids`.

apply_from.description: When the discount becomes active. Defaults to the creation time.

apply_until.description: When the discount expires. `null` means it never expires.

code.description: The code a buyer redeems at checkout. Uppercased on save; unique within the workspace (cannot collide with a coupon code).

currency.description: ISO currency code, lowercased. Defaults to the workspace currency.

discount_method.description: How the discount is calculated. `percentage` uses `percent`; `fixed` uses `amount`. `shipping` and `bogo` exist but are outside the simple flow.

discount_type.description: `code` (the default) is a redeemable coupon code. `automatic` and `sale` are deprecated.

discounts_per_redemption.description: Optional cap on how many line items a single redemption discounts.

expired.description: Derived - true when `apply_until` is in the past. An expired discount is frozen - every further update returns 422, so rename before you expire.

limit_1_per_customer.description: When true, each contact can redeem the discount only once.

percent.description: Percentage off between 0.01 and 100 (e.g. "20.0"). `null` for a fixed discount.

product_ids.description: The products the discount is scoped to (empty unless `applies_to` is `specific_products`).

products_collection_ids.description: The collections the discount is scoped to (empty unless `applies_to` is `specific_collections`).

redemptions_count.description: How many times the discount has been redeemed on an invoice. On Stripe every invoice counts, renewals included; on Payments AI each customer redemption counts once, however many renewal invoices it covers. This is not a deletability signal - a discount can report zero redemptions and still return 422 on DELETE because it is applied to an order that has no invoice yet.

require_minimum_spend.description: When true, the order must meet `require_minimum_spend_amount` for the discount to apply.

require_minimum_spend_amount.description: Minimum order subtotal required, when `require_minimum_spend` is true. In whole currency units, not cents - `50` on a `usd` discount means $50.

scheduled.description: Derived - true when `apply_from` is in the future.

variant_ids.description: The variants the discount is scoped to (empty unless `applies_to` is `specific_variants`).

DiscountAttributes.title: Discount

DiscountParameters.description: Fields accepted when creating a discount.

amount.description: Fixed amount off as a decimal string. Required when `discount_method` is `fixed`.

apply_from.description: When the discount becomes active. Defaults to now. Set in the future to schedule it.

apply_until.description: When the discount expires. Omit for no expiry. There is no `expired` create field - sending one returns 422 whatever its value, including `false`, because expiring on create can never succeed (it would set `apply_until` to now, and `apply_from` then defaults to a hair later). Create the discount first, then expire it with `PATCH { "discount": { "expired": true } }`.

code.description: Required for a `code`-type discount. Letters, numbers and hyphens only - spaces, underscores and punctuation return 422. Uppercased on save; must be unique within the workspace (it cannot collide with a coupon code either).

currency.description: ISO currency code. Defaults to the workspace currency.

discount_method.description: Defaults to `percentage`. `percentage` requires `percent`; `fixed` requires a positive `amount`.

product_ids.description: Product ids to scope to, when `applies_to` is `specific_products`.

products_collection_ids.description: Collection ids to scope to, when `applies_to` is `specific_collections`.

require_minimum_spend_amount.description: Minimum order subtotal, in whole currency units rather than cents - `50` on a `usd` discount means $50. Must be positive when `require_minimum_spend` is true.

variant_ids.description: Variant ids to scope to, when `applies_to` is `specific_variants`.

DiscountParameters.title: Discount

DiscountParametersUpdate.description: Fields accepted when updating a discount. Two lock-out rules apply, in this order: once the discount has been redeemed on an order its money-affecting fields (amount, percent, discount_method, applies_to, apply_from, the scoping arrays, limit_1_per_customer, discounts_per_redemption) are locked and return 422, while renaming and expiring still work; a discount that is already expired freezes its other fields and returns 422 (`Discount cannot be changed because it has expired`). Expiring is reversible - `expired: false` clears the end date and a future `apply_until` pushes it out, either of which makes the discount live again - so editing an expired discount means lifting the expiry first. Expiring a discount and renaming it in the same request is fine; it is a rename sent to a discount that is already expired that gets refused.

apply_until.description: Schedule a future end date. Must be after `apply_from`; a past date returns 422. To expire a live discount now, use `expired: true` instead.

code.description: Letters, numbers and hyphens only. Uppercased on save; must be unique within the workspace.

currency.description: ISO currency code. Locked once the discount has been applied to an order.

discount_type.description: `code` is a redeemable coupon code. `automatic` and `sale` are deprecated.

expired.description: Virtual switch over `apply_until`, accepted on update only (sending it on create returns 422). `true` expires the discount immediately by setting `apply_until` to now; `false` lifts an expiry by clearing `apply_until`, the same as Remove Expiration in the app. It ends a discount that has not started yet (`scheduled: true`) as well, discarding the future `apply_from`, since nothing can end before it starts. A discount that has been redeemed cannot be un-expired and returns 422. Sending the state the discount is already in changes nothing and returns 200 without moving `apply_until`, so echoing a serialized discount back in a routine update cannot clear a scheduled end date - to remove a future end date, PATCH `apply_until` to null instead. Only `true` and `false` are accepted; any other value returns 422 rather than being read as "expire it".

require_minimum_spend_amount.description: Minimum order subtotal, in whole currency units rather than cents - `50` on a `usd` discount means $50.

DnsRecord.description: A single DNS record to add at the domain's DNS provider to configure email transport (or, for the return path, bounce handling).

name.description: The DNS host/name to create the record on (e.g. `example.com` or `_dmarc.example.com`).

ttl.description: Recommended TTL, in seconds, for the record.

value.description: The exact value to paste at the registrar for this record.

verified.description: Whether this specific record has been confirmed live at the DNS provider. It reflects stored DNS verification state; call `verifyEmailsDomains` to re-check.

DnsRecord.title: DNS Record

connected.description: Whether the domain is fully connected and active

public_id.description: The public identifier of the domain

status.description: The current connection status of the domain

workspace_id.description: The ID of the workspace that the domain belongs to

asset_id.description: The Asset ID to pass in `product_variant.asset_ids` when granting this download through a product variant.

image_id.description: ID of the workspace image shown with the download, for example in the Customer Center.

permanent_url.description: The file's permanent link, the same one the app's copy-link button gives. Put it in pages and emails as is. It does not expire, and each visit redirects to a short-lived download of the file. Replacing the download's file gives it a new link. Null when no file is attached.

image_id.description: Numeric or public ID of a workspace image to show with the download, for example in the Customer Center.

name.description: Optional; defaults to the downloaded filename without its extension.

upload_source_url.description: Public URL of the file. It is fetched while the request runs, following redirects, and can be up to 100 MB; a source too slow to finish within the request is refused. Executable and script files are refused.

emails_domain.description: Sending-domain verification status for this address. `null` for shared-domain / workspace-default addresses, which send via shared infrastructure and have no per-workspace sending domain.

dkim_verified.description: Whether the domain's DKIM DNS record is verified.

dmarc_verified.description: Whether the domain's DMARC DNS record is verified.

smtp_verified.description: Whether the domain is verified via a verified SMTP setting (an alternative to DNS verification). A domain is `verified` when its DKIM/SPF/DMARC are all verified OR `smtp_verified` is true — so when a domain is SMTP-verified, `verified` is true while dkim_verified/spf_verified/dmarc_verified are false.

spf_verified.description: Whether the domain's SPF DNS record is verified.

verified.description: Whether the sending domain has completed transport verification (DKIM/SPF/DMARC DNS records, or a verified SMTP setting). This alone does not mean the address can send; select senders on the address's top-level `usable_as_sender` field.

is_workspace_default.description: Whether this address is on the shared ClickFunnels sending domain (the workspace default). A workspace-default address is usable as a sender only as a fallback: once the workspace has a usable custom sender of its own, its workspace-default address reports `usable_as_sender: false`. So `is_workspace_default: true` together with `usable_as_sender: false` is expected whenever the workspace already has a usable custom sender.

name.description: Display name associated with this email address

usable_as_sender.description: Whether this address is eligible to be used as the `from` sender of an email broadcast. A custom-domain address is usable once its sending domain is verified (DKIM/SPF/DMARC or a verified SMTP setting) and the workspace owns that domain. A workspace-default (shared-domain) address is usable only as a fallback - it is `true` when the workspace has no usable custom sender of its own and flips to `false` once one exists. Filter broadcast senders to addresses where this is true to avoid a broadcast failing validation at send time. See [Addresses (pick a usable sender)](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/emails/skill.md#addresses-pick-a-usable-sender) in the [Emails Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/emails/skill.md).

domain.description: Selects among ClickFunnels' shared sending domains only; normally omit it to get the default (`clickfunnelsmail.com`). This is not how you use your own domain: putting a custom name here neither provisions nor authenticates it, and the request is rejected with `422` unless `emails_domain_id` is also given. To send from your own domain, provision it first and pass its numeric id as `emails_domain_id`, which is what the address is then created on.

emails_domain_id.description: Numeric `id` (not `public_id`) of a custom sending domain belonging to this workspace. Use the Email Domains endpoints to provision it and wait until that domain is ready to send before sending from the resulting address.

name.description: The from-name shown to recipients (e.g. "Acme Support"). Required when creating.

username.description: The local part before the @ (e.g. "hello" for hello@yourdomain.com). Required when creating.

external_id.description: An optional external identifier for tracking purposes

filter_id.description: The contact filter determining which contacts receive this broadcast. Numeric `Refine::StoredFilter` id (not the public id) — the broadcast's own unnamed copy of the filter, created automatically from the `filter_id` (or `recipients`) supplied on create/update. `null` until an audience is set. See [Applying filters to email broadcasts](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#applying-filters-to-email-broadcasts).

from_name.description: The sender display name associated with the from address

origination_channel_id.description: The ID of the origination channel

origination_channel_type.description: The type of origination channel that created this broadcast

preheadline.description: Preview text shown in email clients before opening (max 150 characters)

send_at_local_time.description: Scheduled send time in HH:MM:SS format, relative to the specified time zone

send_immediately.description: Whether the broadcast sends immediately upon creation

smart_sending.description: Whether Smart Sending is on. When on, the broadcast is delivered gradually across a window instead of all at once, which protects deliverability. Defaults to `true`, so a broadcast batches unless you explicitly send `smart_sending: false`. Above 5,000 recipients Smart Sending is mandatory: the API may coerce `false` to `true`, and the send batches at that size regardless of the stored value.

smart_sending_time.description: How many `smart_sending_unit`s the delivery window spans. `null` means no override is stored and the window is sized from the audience instead.

smart_sending_unit.description: The unit of the Smart Sending delivery window. `null` means no override is stored and the window is sized from the audience instead.

split_test.description: Whether this broadcast is a subject-line split test. When true, a `split_test_percentage` share of the audience is split evenly across the `variants`; after `split_test_wait_time` hours the variant with the most opens wins and the rest of the audience receives it.

split_test_percentage.description: Share of the audience (0-100) used for the test sends. This can remain populated while a configured test is disabled, and is `null` when no percentage has been configured.

split_test_wait_time.description: Hours to wait after the test sends before the winner is picked. This can remain populated while a configured test is disabled, and is `null` when no wait time has been configured.

status.description: Current broadcast status. New broadcasts start as draft.

subject.description: Email subject line seen by recipients

template.description: A lean reference to the email template this broadcast uses (a broadcast points at a template; it does not copy it, unlike a workflow send-email step). Null when no template is attached. The template's rendered body is not inlined here — fetch it from the templates endpoint via this public_id: GET /api/v2/emails/templates/{public_id}?expand[]=html_body.

topic_ids.description: IDs of topics associated with this broadcast

variants.description: The subject-line variants, oldest first. The main variant mirrors the broadcast's own subject and preheadline. A disabled test can retain an inactive alternate for later editing. A broadcast created before subject-line split tests existed and already sent has none, so the array can be empty; its subject line is then only on the broadcast's own `subject` and `preheadline`.

main.description: Whether this is the main variant, the one that mirrors the broadcast's subject and preheadline. It wins ties.

open_count.description: Opens counted for this variant while the test was running. Frozen when the winner is picked, so it is not the broadcast's overall open count.

preheadline.description: Preview text sent to this variant's share of the audience

send_percentage.description: Share of the audience (0-100) this variant is sent to during the test. Only meaningful when `split_test` is true. Until a `split_test_percentage` is set, the whole audience is split evenly across the variants, as the dashboard reports it.

subject.description: Subject line sent to this variant's share of the audience

winner.description: `null` while the test is still running, and for a broadcast that is not a split test. Once the test closes, `true` for the variant with the most opens (the main variant on a tie) and `false` for the others.

external_id.description: An optional external identifier for your own tracking

filter_id.description: Contact filter for the broadcast audience. Accepts any of three forms: the numeric `id` or the public id (string) of a saved contact filter (`Refine::StoredFilter`) in this workspace, or a serialized contact filter. The supplied filter is copied onto the broadcast — the broadcast points at its own copy, so later edits to (or deletion of) the saved filter never change this broadcast's audience. Saved contact filters can be created/listed via the [Refine Filters Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md). If `recipients` are provided instead, a filter is created automatically from them and takes precedence over `filter_id`. See [Applying filters to email broadcasts](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#applying-filters-to-email-broadcasts).

from_email.description: Sender email address. Required on create. Must be an email address that belongs to the workspace, and it must have `usable_as_sender: true` or the send is rejected with 422. Do not pick by the sending domain's `verified` flag: that covers email transport only. See GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/emails/addresses, where a shared workspace-default address is usable only while the workspace has no ready custom sender.

html_body.description: HTML email body. If provided without a template_id, a template is automatically created from this content.

preheadline.description: Preview text shown in email clients before opening. Maximum 150 characters.

recipients.description: List of recipients (maximum 1,000). Contacts are created or matched by email address.

reply_to_email.description: Reply-to email address. Must be an address in the workspace if provided. Pick one whose `usable_as_sender` is `true`.

send_at.description: Scheduled send date. Required when send_immediately is false.

send_at_local_time.description: Scheduled send time in HH:MM:SS format. Defaults to 18:00:00.

send_immediately.description: Set to true to send the broadcast immediately upon creation. If false, use send_at, send_at_local_time, and time_zone to schedule.

smart_sending.description: Smart Sending. When true the broadcast is delivered gradually across a window rather than all at once, which protects deliverability. **Defaults to `true`**: send `false` explicitly to deliver the whole audience in one go. Above 5,000 recipients Smart Sending is mandatory: sending `false` is accepted and may be stored as `true`. The send batches at that size regardless of the stored value.

smart_sending_time.description: How many `smart_sending_unit`s the delivery window spans, for example `2` with `hour`. Must be between 0.5 and 100, and must be sent together with `smart_sending_unit`. Omit both to size the window from the audience, which is the recommended default.

smart_sending_unit.description: The unit of the Smart Sending delivery window. Must be sent together with `smart_sending_time`. Omit both to size the window from the audience, which is the recommended default.

split_test.description: Enable a subject-line split test. Requires exactly one alternate in `variants`. When enabled without stored settings, percentage defaults to 100 and wait time defaults to 0 hours. Must be a JSON boolean - string spellings such as `"true"` return 422.

split_test_percentage.description: Whole-number share of the audience used for the test sends. The share is divided evenly between variant A and variant B.

split_test_wait_time.description: Whole hours to wait before choosing the subject-line winner.

subject.description: Email subject line seen by recipients

template_id.description: Numeric id of an existing email template in this workspace to use. Alternative to providing html_body/text_body directly; takes precedence when both are given. The broadcast references this template (it is not copied).

time_zone.description: Time zone for scheduling (defaults to workspace time zone)

topic_ids.description: Topic IDs to associate. Only topics belonging to the workspace are accepted.

variants.description: Zero or one alternate subject-line variant B. The top-level subject and preheadline are variant A. Supplying B does not enable testing by itself.

preheadline.description: Preview text for variant B. Omit or send null to clear it.

EmailsBroadcastParametersUpdate.description: Email Broadcasts. Only draft broadcasts can be updated.

external_id.description: An optional external identifier for your own tracking

filter_id.description: Contact filter for the broadcast audience. Accepts any of three forms: the numeric `id` or the public id (string) of a saved contact filter (`Refine::StoredFilter`) in this workspace, or a serialized contact filter. The supplied filter is copied onto the broadcast — the broadcast points at its own copy, so later edits to (or deletion of) the saved filter never change this broadcast's audience. Saved contact filters can be created/listed via the [Refine Filters Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md). See [Applying filters to email broadcasts](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#applying-filters-to-email-broadcasts).

from_email.description: Sender email address. Must be a verified email address that belongs to the workspace.

preheadline.description: Preview text shown in email clients before opening. Maximum 150 characters.

reply_to_email.description: Reply-to email address. Must be a verified address in the workspace if provided.

send_at_local_time.description: Scheduled send time in HH:MM:SS format

send_immediately.description: Whether the broadcast is set to send immediately rather than at its scheduled date and time. Setting it to false requires `send_at` (in this request or already on the broadcast). Creating a send action overrides this either way - see `createEmailsBroadcastsSendActions`.

smart_sending.description: Smart Sending. When true the broadcast is delivered gradually across a window rather than all at once, which protects deliverability. A broadcast is created with this on, so send `false` to deliver the whole audience in one go. Above 5,000 recipients Smart Sending is mandatory: sending `false` is accepted and may be stored as `true`. The send batches at that size regardless of the stored value.

smart_sending_time.description: How many `smart_sending_unit`s the delivery window spans, for example `2` with `hour`. Must be between 0.5 and 100, and must be sent together with `smart_sending_unit`. Send both as `null` to go back to sizing the window from the audience.

smart_sending_unit.description: The unit of the Smart Sending delivery window. Must be sent together with `smart_sending_time`. Send both as `null` to go back to sizing the window from the audience.

split_test.description: Enable or disable the subject-line split test. Disabling preserves variant B and the stored test settings for later editing. Must be a JSON boolean - string spellings such as `"true"` return 422.

split_test_percentage.description: Whole-number share of the audience used for the test sends. Omit to preserve the stored value.

split_test_wait_time.description: Whole hours to wait before choosing the subject-line winner. Omit to preserve the stored value.

subject.description: Email subject line seen by recipients

template_id.description: Numeric id of an existing email template in this workspace to point this draft broadcast at (swaps the referenced template). Takes precedence over an inline html_body/text_body. Only draft broadcasts can be updated; an unknown id returns 422.

variants.description: Omit to preserve variant B, send one entry to replace B, or send an empty array to remove B while split_test is false. The top-level subject and preheadline remain variant A.

preheadline.description: Replacement preview text for variant B. Omit or send null to clear it.

subject.description: Replacement subject line for variant B.

FilterResults.description:
The records the filter matches, returned inline so selecting a set and reading it is one
call instead of a filter plus a paginated crawl.

**Column-oriented.** `fields` states the column order once and `rows` carries bare value
arrays. Repeating every key on every record roughly doubles the payload for a projection
of a few scalars, which defeats the purpose of asking for a projection. Zip `fields` with
each row to reconstruct objects.

`truncated` tells you whether `rows` is the whole set. A total `count` is present only
when the request opts in with `results.count: true`, because counting a truncated set
requires a second evaluation of the filter. Use the workspace stats endpoint when you
need only a number.

Saved contact and order filters support `results`. Other filter classes return 422 until
the API defines an explicit projection allow-list for them.

**You set the budget; the response tells you what it cost.** How much a client can absorb
is not something this API can know, so `results.max_bytes` and `results.limit` are yours to
set and their defaults (3 KB of rows, 500 rows) are only a conservative starting point. Every
response reports estimated `bytes`, `bytes_per_record` and the `max_bytes` actually applied,
so one call is enough to size every call after it. These estimates are measured before final
response encoding, which can be slightly larger for values such as timestamps; leave headroom.
When a response is `truncated`,
`suggested_max_bytes` is the value to retry with to get the whole set in one call
(extrapolated from the widest row RETURNED SO FAR, so it can still undershoot if later
records are wider - check `truncated` again on the retry), and `guidance` spells
out the alternatives. The only ceiling you cannot raise is the server's own
(4 MB of rows per response), which protects the server rather than your context; past it,
page with `next_after` or narrow the filter.

**`max_bytes` bounds the ROWS, not the whole response.** Over MCP the payload is carried twice
(structured plus text mirror) alongside the filter definition, which measured at 2.0x-2.9x the
rows on the wire. So when sizing against a client tool-result cap, divide by ~3. The default is
already sized that way. `suggested_max_bytes` comes back in the same rows units, so it can be
passed straight back.

bytes.description: Estimated serialized size of `rows`, measured before final response encoding. Values such as timestamps can make the wire representation slightly larger, so leave headroom.

bytes_per_record.description: Average estimated bytes per returned record, so you can size a later call for a different record count.

count.description: Present only when `results.count` was true. Total records the filter matches, independent of the current page. Computed like the workspace stats count: exact, including past the 100,000-record scan cap, unless counting the whole set cannot finish within the time budget, in which case it reports the cap with `count_capped_at`. Counting a truncated result requires a second evaluation of the filter.

count_capped_at.description: Present only when `count` saturated at the scan cap the server applies and counting the whole set could not finish in time: the real total is HIGHER than `count`, so treat `count` as a floor rather than a total. Narrow the filter to get an exact number. Absent means `count` is exact. Same marker the workspace stats endpoint returns for the same case.

count_unavailable_reason.description: Present only when `results.count` was true but its additional filter evaluation could not complete within the filtered-query time budget. The rows, truncation signal, and continuation cursor are still valid; narrow the filter or use the workspace stats endpoint for the count.

fields.description: The projected field names, in the order the values appear in each row.

guidance.description:
Present only when `truncated` is true: what to do about it, cheapest-first — retry with
`suggested_max_bytes` to get everything in one call, raise your own `limit`, narrow the
filter, project fewer `fields`, page with `next_after` (including how many calls that
will take at this size when `count` is available), export the full set as a CSV, or use
the workspace stats endpoint if a number is all that was wanted. The export option is only offered when the filtered
resource actually has a bulk export and the calling token could create one, so neither an
order filter nor a read-only connection is pointed at something that would fail.

max_bytes.description: The pre-response row-cost budget applied — your `results.max_bytes` after clamping to the server ceiling, or the default when you didn't set one. It is not an exact wire-size ceiling; leave headroom.

next_after.description: Cursor to continue from, present only when `truncated` is true. Pass it back as `results[after]`. It is the id of the last row actually RETURNED, so paging never skips a record the budget dropped.

rows.description: One array of values per matching record, ordered by id. Each value renders the way the resource's own serializer renders that column, so a money field such as `total_amount` arrives as a string at the currency's minor units (`"100.00"`) and can be compared with the same field read from the record endpoint. A `null` means the column has no value for that record.

stop_reason.description: Present only when `truncated`: which ceiling stopped us, so you do not have to parse `guidance` to find out. `row_limit` means raise your own `limit`; `byte_budget` means raise `max_bytes` or project fewer fields; `record_exceeds_budget` means a single record is larger than the whole budget, so project fewer fields. `time_budget` is the only one you cannot lift: the request reached its filtered-query wall-clock budget, so page with `next_after` or narrow the filter -- raising `max_bytes` or `limit` will not help, because neither is what stopped it.

suggested_max_bytes.description: Present only when `results.count` was true, the response is `truncated`, and the whole set could fit in one response: the `results.max_bytes` to retry with to get all `count` records in a single call. Extrapolated from the widest row returned SO FAR, not the average — so it is an estimate, and a later record wider than anything on this page can still make the retry truncate. Check `truncated` on the retry rather than assuming it is whole. Absent when the set is too large for any single response, when no exact total was requested or known, or when the wall-clock budget stopped the request — then page or narrow instead.

truncated.description: True when `rows` is a page rather than the whole set, because the rows reached `limit` or `max_bytes`, or the request reached its filtered-query wall-clock budget.

FilterResultsParameter.description: Return projected matches inline. Pass `true` for ids only; omit for the filter definition alone.

count.description: Include the bounded total count. May require another filter evaluation.

max_bytes.description: Caller-set row byte budget. Defaults to 3072 and is capped at 4194304.

OrderParameters.description:
Parameters for creating external orders. External orders are orders managed outside of ClickFunnels payment processors (Payments AI or Stripe).

**Required fields:**
- `order_type`: Must be `one-time-order` or `subscription-order`
- `live_mode`: Must be `true` or `false`
- `contact_id` or `contact_attributes`: Either provide a `contact_id` directly, or use `contact_attributes` with an `email_address` to look up an existing contact
- `line_items_attributes`: At least one line item with `variant_id`, `products_price_id`, and `quantity`

**Note:** For one-time orders, line items must reference one-time products. For subscription orders, line items can include both one-time and subscription products.

`pending`, `draft`, `paid`, `unpaid`, `partially-refunded`, `refunded`, `voided`, `disputed`, `past-due`.

Possible codes for Payments AI orders are:
`did-not-use`, `did-not-want`, `missing-features`, `too-expensive`, `bugs-or-problems`, `other`

Possible codes for Stripe orders are:

External orders accept the same cancelation reasons as Stripe.

Either `contact_id` or `contact_attributes` must be provided, but not both.
If both are provided, `contact_id` takes precedence.

products_price_id.description: The ID of the price for the product. Must be a valid price for the variant's product.

service_status.description:
The service status reflects the activity state of the order. For subscriptions, it can control whether a subscription is ongoing, for example despite an irregular (unpaid) invoice status.

For orders with Payments AI as the payment processor, it can be one of the following:
`pending`, `active`, `completed`, `churned`, `canceled`, `suspended`, `paused`, `abandoned`, `voided`
Stripe orders have the same order statuses, except for `voided`. For voided invoices, its service status becomes `abandoned`.
You can read about the state transitions in more detail in our [orders overview guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/orders).

For external one-time orders possible service statuses are `pending` or `completed`. For external subscription orders possible statuses are `pending`, `active`, `churned`, `canceled`, `completed`, `paused`.

OrderParametersCancel.description:
Parameters for `POST /orders/{id}/cancel`. All fields are optional — a bare POST (or
`{"order": {}}`) cancels the subscription order with defaults.

This routes the cancelation through ClickFunnels' own cancel path (the same path the
in-app "Cancel subscription" flow uses) so it propagates to the payment processor
(Payments AI/Rebilly or Stripe). A direct `PATCH` of `service_status` to `canceled` is a
no-op for processor-managed orders, which is why this action exists. Only Payments AI
and Stripe subscription orders can be canceled this way; calling it on a one-time order
or an external subscription returns a 422.

cancel_description.description: A free-text description of the cancellation reason.

cancel_reason.description:
The reason _code_ for the cancelation. Defaults to `other`. Valid values are
processor-specific; a value that isn't accepted for the order's processor returns a 422.

Stripe orders accept:
`customer_service`, `low_quality`, `missing_features`, `other`, `switched_service`, `too_complex`, `too_expensive`, `unused`

Payments AI (Rebilly) orders accept:
`did-not-use`, `did-not-want`, `missing-features`, `too-expensive`, `bugs-or-problems`, `other`

cancelation_proration.description: Whether to prorate the cancelation. Defaults to `false`.

canceled_by.description: Attribution for who or what requested the cancelation. It is persisted on the order and recorded in its audit timeline. Defaults to `API`.

effective_date.description:
When the cancelation takes effect.
- `next_renewal`: cancels at the end of the current paid period. Access is retained until `paid_until`.
- Any other value: cancels immediately.

When omitted, it cancels immediately if the order's current period was never paid for
(`billing_status` is `unpaid`, `past-due`, `delinquent`, `failed`, `voided`, `abandoned`
or `disputed`), and at `next_renewal` otherwise.

See [Cancel a subscription](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/orders/skill.md#cancel-a-subscription) in the [Orders Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/orders/skill.md) for
how the period-end and immediate cancels differ and which fields settle later.

voidable_invoices.description:
IDs of the order's invoices to void as part of the cancelation. When omitted, all of the
order's open (`unpaid` or `past-due`) invoices are voided, so the payment processor stops
retrying them. Send `[]` to keep them open. Any other value, such as `null` or a single id
outside an array, returns a 422.

renewal_at.description:
Set the next billing-cycle start for a Payments AI subscription in `pending`, `active`, or
`paused` state using an absolute RFC 3339 timestamp within the next two years.
This moves the next billing attempt without changing the amount or prorating it.

A renewal cannot precede a future trial end. Send both fields with the same timestamp to end
the trial and bill then. To renew later, update `trial_end_at` first, re-read the order until
it shows the effective new trial end, then update `renewal_at`.

(External orders only) The service status reflects the activity state of the order.
For external one-time orders possible service statuses are `pending` or `completed`.
For external subscription orders possible statuses are `pending`, `active`, `churned`, `canceled`, `completed`, `paused`.

shipping_address_phone_number.description: (External orders only) The phone number of the recipient's shipping address.

shipping_address_postal_code.description: (External orders only) The postal code of the shipping address.

shipping_address_region.description: (External orders only) The region of the shipping address, like state or province.

shipping_address_street_one.description: (External orders only) The main street information of the shipping address, including the street name and number.

shipping_address_street_two.description: (External orders only) Additional street information for the shipping address, like entrance information and apartment numbers.

trial_end_at.description:
Set the trial end for a Payments AI or Stripe subscription as an absolute RFC 3339 timestamp.
A later value extends the trial and an earlier future value shortens it. The order normally
has `in_trial: true`; Payments AI also accepts `trial_end_at` as the equal companion to a
legal `renewal_at` move while the stored trial end is still in the future.

The timestamp must include a date, time, and UTC offset and be within the next two years.
Moving the trial end also moves the first charge. Send a timestamp a few seconds ahead to
end the trial now.

OrdersInvoiceParameters.description:
Parameters for creating an external invoice. Only external orders support invoice creation via the API.
External orders are orders where payments are processed outside of ClickFunnels.

due_at.description: The date the invoice is due.

external_id.description:
Required. A unique identifier for this invoice in your external system.
This ID allows you to correlate ClickFunnels invoices with records in your payment processor.

invoice_number.description:
Optional. A sequential number for bookkeeping purposes.
If not provided, one will be auto-generated.

invoice_type.description:
The type of invoice. If not provided, defaults based on the order type:
- For one-time orders: `one_time_sale`
- For subscription orders: `initial`

For subscription orders, valid types are: `initial`, `renewal`, `interim`, `cancellation`, `one_time`, `refund`, `charge`.
For one-time orders, only `one_time_sale` is valid.

issued_at.description: The date the invoice was issued.

line_items_attributes.description:
Line items for the invoice. Each line item represents a product/variant being invoiced.
Required fields for each line item: `amount`, `quantity`, `variant_id`, `products_price_id`.

amount.description: The price amount for this line item.

description.description: Optional description for the line item.

paid_at.description: The date the invoice was paid. Required when `status` is `paid`.

shipping_amount.description: Invoiced shipping amount. Cannot be negative. Defaults to "0.00".

status.description:
Required. The billing status of the invoice.

For external one-time orders, valid statuses are: `unpaid`, `paid`, `voided`, `refunded`, `disputed`, `past-due`.
For external subscription orders, the same statuses apply.

When creating an invoice with status `paid`, you must also provide `paid_at`.
A change in status will update the `billing_status` of the parent order.
If a one-time order's invoice status is changed to `paid`, the order's `service_status` will also flip to `completed`.

Represents the current fulfillment status of the line item.
This can be one of the following:
 - `unfulfilled` - the line item has not been fully fulfilled (fulfilled quantity is 0)
 - `partially_fulfilled` - the line item is partially fulfilled (fulfilled quantity is less than line item quantity)
 - `complete` - the line item is completely fulfilled (fulfilled quantity is equal to line item quantity)
 - `ignored` - the line item is marked as ignored for fulfillment

description.description: The description of the variant. The description of the **default variant** is the user-facing description of the `Product`.

products_variant.name: Seinfeld In Your Pocket - Comedy Joke Machine (Black Premium)

description.description: The description of the variant. The description of the **default variant** is the user-facing description of the `Product`.

OrdersLineItemsChangeRequest.description: Parameters to preview or commit a subscription line item variant/price change

effective_time.description:
Optional override for when the change takes effect. When omitted (or `null`,
or an empty string), the in-app default is used: upgrades take effect now,
downgrades at the next renewal. Any other value (e.g. `end_of_period` or a
literal timestamp) returns 422.

products_price_id.description:
Target price. Accepts either the integer database id or the obfuscated
`public_id` string returned by the discovery endpoint. The target variant is
derived from the price's `variant` association.

prorate.description:
Optional override for proration. Accepts `true`, `false`, `"true"`, `"false"`,
`"1"`, `"0"`, `1`, or `0`. When omitted, the in-app default is used:
upgrades are prorated and applied immediately; downgrades are not prorated and
take effect at the end of the current billing cycle. Forced to `false` for
physical line items regardless of the value sent. Any other value returns 422.

OrdersLineItemsChangeRequest.title: Line Item Change Request

OrdersLineItemsChangeResponse.description:
Result of a subscription line item variant/price change. The same envelope is returned
for both preview and commit endpoints — the `preview` flag indicates which.

`upcoming_invoice` is a snapshot of the upcoming-invoice impact of the change as quoted
by the upstream payment platform. It is **informational** — the line item is mutated
regardless of whether the quote succeeds. On commit, the quote is snapshotted just
before the change is applied so consumers don't need a separate preview round-trip
to know what their customer will be charged. Individual amount fields may be `null`
if the upstream quote returned no data; `currency` and `next_invoice_date` fall back
to the order's stored currency and renewal date in that case.

new_line_item.description:
The line item as it would be after the change (preview) or as it now is after
the change (commit) — same `id` as the current line item, with `products_price`
and `products_variant` reflecting the target.

preview.description:
`true` for the preview endpoint, `false` for the commit endpoint. The remainder
of the envelope is shaped identically; the flag lets clients render the same UI
or write the same parsing code for both calls.

previous_line_item.description:
The line item as it was before the change — same `id` as the current line item,
but with `products_price` and `products_variant` reflecting the pre-change
target.

upcoming_invoice.description:
Snapshot of the upcoming-invoice impact of the change as quoted by the upstream
payment platform. Populated on both preview and commit (commit snapshots a quote
inside the change transaction so the response carries the same fields as preview).
Informational only — the line item change is committed regardless of whether the
quote succeeds.

currency.description:
Currency of the upcoming invoice quote. Falls back to the order's stored
currency if the quote returned no data.

discount_amount.description: Upcoming invoice discount quoted by the payment platform. `null` if the quote returned no data.

next_invoice_date.description:
Upcoming invoice date as quoted by the payment platform. Falls back to the
order's stored renewal date if the quote returned no data.

shipping_amount.description: Upcoming invoice shipping quoted by the payment platform. `null` if the quote returned no data.

subtotal_amount.description: Upcoming invoice subtotal quoted by the payment platform. `null` if the quote returned no data.

tax_amount.description: Upcoming invoice tax quoted by the payment platform. `null` if the quote returned no data.

total_amount.description: Upcoming invoice total quoted by the payment platform. `null` if the quote returned no data.

OrdersLineItemsChangeResponse.title: Line Item Change

status.description: Status

OrdersTransactionParametersRefund.description:
Parameters for `POST /orders/transactions/{id}/refund`. Every field is optional - a bare POST
(or `{"orders_transaction": {}}`) refunds the addressed charge with defaults.

The refund is always for the charge's full outstanding amount, so there is no amount to send.
Partial refunds are deliberately not offered here: they are a human-gated exception, handled in
the ClickFunnels admin.

partial.description:
Must be `false` or omitted. Sending `true` returns 422 rather than silently refunding the
full charge. An `amount` field is rejected the same way - honoring it would be a partial
refund, and ignoring it would refund more than you asked for.

reason.description:
Defaults to `requested_by_customer`.

Stripe orders accept only `duplicate`, `fraudulent`, or `requested_by_customer`; any other
value returns 422 listing the accepted set. Payments AI (Rebilly) orders treat this as a
free-text description that is recorded on the refund and the order timeline.

OrdersTransactionParametersRefund.title: Refund Transaction

block_ai_assistant.description: Whether AI assistants (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User and others) are blocked from opening this page when a person asks them to — for example pasting the page's link into a chat. Defaults to false. Enforced via robots.txt. block_ai_crawler.description: Whether AI training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot and others) are blocked from using this page's content to train models. Defaults to false. Enforced by a `Disallow` rule in the domain's robots.txt — see [Crawler access (AI opt-out)](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#crawler-access-ai-opt-out) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md) for coverage limits. Independent of `seo_index` and of the other two AI flags.

block_ai_search.description: Whether AI answer engines (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and others) are blocked from indexing this page and citing it when people ask questions. Defaults to false. Enforced via robots.txt. See [Crawler access (AI opt-out)](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#crawler-access-ai-opt-out) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md) for coverage limits.

current_path.description: The current URL path for the page resource. This is the canonical URL for landing and site pages. `null` for externally-hosted (SDK) pages. **For funnel pages this is NOT the customer-facing URL** — that's `url` (or `show_page_step.current_path` for the path component). The page-level current_path on a funnel page does not route the visitor through the workflow step, so a `<checkout/>` element on it will not see the step's attached products. See [Setting a page's path (`current_path`)](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#setting-a-pages-path-current_path) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md).

custom_css.description: **Expandable** Raw CSS applied at the page level (no <style> wrapper). Maps to the CSS tab in the page editor's Code Editor panel. Internal pages only. Only returned when expand[]=custom_css is provided. Note: expanding may add latency, especially on list endpoints. Use sparingly.

custom_html_page.description: Whether this is a ClickFunnels-hosted custom HTML page — a page whose entire body is author-supplied HTML served verbatim (no page editor, no PML). Read the HTML via `GET /pages/{id}/custom_html` and replace it by sending the write-only `custom_html` string on `PATCH /pages/{id}`. Create these via `POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/pages/custom_html`. (Deliberately named differently from the `custom_html` request field so echoing a GET payload back into PATCH never collides.)

description.description: A short description of the page (max 1000 characters).

footer_code.description: **Expandable** Custom HTML/JavaScript code injected before the closing body tag. Only returned when expand[]=footer_code is provided. Note: expanding may add latency, especially on list endpoints. Use sparingly.

funnel.description: The funnel associated with this page (if the page is part of a funnel)

id.description: The unique identifier of the funnel

public_id.description: The public identifier of the funnel

head_code.description: **Expandable** Custom HTML/JavaScript code injected into the page head section. Only returned when expand[]=head_code is provided. Note: expanding may add latency, especially on list endpoints. Use sparingly.

markup.description: **Expandable** The PML (Page Markup Language) representation of the page's visual tree. Only returned when expand[]=markup is provided. Note: expanding may add latency, especially on list endpoints. This serialization is lossy: elements PML has no equivalent for are omitted with no error and no placeholder, so a round-tripped read is not a safe basis for rewriting a page (see [the approval guardrail](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md#stop-get-approval-before-overwriting-an-existing-page)). An empty string therefore does not prove the page is empty: a page built entirely from elements PML cannot express also reads back empty. The value `<!-- markup unavailable: page tree could not be serialized -->` means the read failed; treat the page as unreadable and do not write that string back. See the [Page Markup Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md) for the full DSL reference.

name.description: Page name of the editable page element. Want to filter by it? See our help guide on that topic.

public_id.description: The public identifier of the page

sdk.description: Present for SDK-enabled pages — externally-hosted (SDK) pages and ClickFunnels-hosted custom HTML pages; `null` for other pages. Contains the SDK integration token, plus the external URL for externally-hosted pages.

external_url.description: The fully-qualified URL of the externally-hosted page. Only present for externally-hosted pages (absent for custom HTML pages, which live on the funnel's own domain).

token.description: The SDK page token (prefixed `cfp_`). Embed this in the page via a `<meta name="cf-page-token" content="<token>">` tag and include the SDK script tag to register the page with ClickFunnels. See [The entire public surface](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/sdk/create-external-page/skill.md#the-entire-public-surface) in the [Create an External Page Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/sdk/create-external-page/skill.md) for the exact tags to paste.

seo_description.description: Custom meta description for search engine results. Falls back to the site's SEO description if not set.

seo_index.description: Whether search engines should index this page. Defaults to false.

seo_title.description: Custom title for search engine results. Falls back to the site's SEO title if not set.

show_page_step.description: The show page step (the workflow step's _function_) associated with this page. The `products` array is the live list of products attached to this step's checkout — main products and order bumps alike, each flagged by its own `bump` field; it is mutated via `show_page_step.product_ids` / `show_page_step.bumps` on page create/update (additive) and `DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/products` (removal).

current_path.description: The current URL path for the step in the funnel. This is the path component of the live, customer-facing URL for funnel pages. `null` for externally-hosted (SDK) pages.

id.description: The ID of the show page step (function). Pass this as `show_page_step_id` when positioning split-test or conditional-split steps via `/api/v2/funnels/:id/split_test_steps` and `/api/v2/funnels/:id/conditional_split_steps`.

name.description: The name of the step in the funnel. This is the page name that is visible in the funnel builder for a show page step.

products.description: Products currently attached to this step's checkout, main products and order bumps together in display order. Mutated via `show_page_step.product_ids` (main) and `show_page_step.bumps` (bumps) on page create/update (additive) and `DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/products` (removal, either kind).

bump.description: Whether this product is attached as an **order bump** (an optional add-on offered next to the main products) rather than a main product. `true` for products served to `<checkout/>` and to the SDK as `bumpProducts`. Set via `show_page_step.bumps` on page create/update.

bump_preheadline.description: The short line of copy shown above this order bump's offer, when one was set via that bump's `preheadline` in `show_page_step.bumps`. Always `null` for products that are not bumps.

public_id.description: The public identifier of the show page step (function). May be passed as `show_page_step_id` alongside other `public_id` references in your code.

sort_order.description: The zero-based position of this step within the funnel. The first step is 0, the second is 1, and so on. Returned in every page response; pass `sort_order` on create/update to control positioning.

type.description: The type of page. Can be one of `landing_page`, `site_page`, `funnel_page` or `theme_page`. May be `null` for a page that matches none of these categories.

url.description: The customer-facing URL for the page on the live site. For funnel pages this routes through the workflow step (which feeds `<checkout/>` its IncludedProducts). Always prefer this over `current_path` when constructing links.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID that the page belongs to.
