current_path.description: The URL path for the page. If left blank, a randomized path will be generated. When attaching to a funnel, this value becomes the ShowPageStep path (the user-facing URL), and the page's own current_path will be set to a randomized value with a suffix, since the ShowPageStep path is the source of truth for funnel pages. See [Setting a page's path (`current_path`)](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#setting-a-pages-path-current_path) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md) for the path rules.

custom_css.description: Raw CSS to apply at the page level (no <style> wrapper). Maps to the CSS tab in the page editor's Code Editor panel. Internal pages only. Set to null to clear existing CSS.

custom_css_mode.description: How to handle custom_css. 'append' adds to existing CSS (default), 'replace' overwrites.

description.description: A short description of the page (max 1000 characters).

footer_code.description: Custom code to inject before the closing </body> tag. JavaScript should be wrapped in <script> tags. Set to null to clear existing code.

footer_code_mode.description: How to handle footer_code. 'append' adds to existing code (default), 'replace' overwrites.

funnel.description: Optional funnel association. Use either funnel_id (to create a new step) or show_page_step_id (to attach to existing step). If both are provided, show_page_step_id takes precedence and funnel_id is ignored.

after_show_page_step_id.description:
Controls where the new step is inserted within the funnel (only relevant when `funnel_id` is provided). Accepts either:
- A ShowPageStep `id` (the function id, as exposed under `show_page_step.id` in page responses) — inserts the new step immediately after the referenced show page step.
- The workflow root step's id (integer) — inserts the new step at the beginning of the funnel.
If omitted or null, the page is appended after the currently last step of the funnel. Returns 400 if the id does not resolve to a valid step in the funnel.

funnel_id.description: The public ID of the funnel to attach this page to. A new show page step will be created as the last step of the funnel, unless `after_show_page_step_id` is provided.

show_page_step_id.description: The ID of an existing show page step to attach this page to. Takes precedence over funnel_id if both are provided.

head_code.description: Custom code to inject into the page's <head> section. Content should be wrapped in appropriate HTML tags such as <script>, <link>, <meta>, or <style>. Set to null to clear existing code.

head_code_mode.description: How to handle head_code. 'append' adds to existing code (default), 'replace' overwrites.

markup.description: A valid PML (Page Markup Language) string that replaces the page's visual tree. Page metadata (name, path, SEO settings) is preserved. Markup that stops mid-construct (a tag, attribute value, comment or `<customhtml>` body that never closes, or elements still open at the end of the document) is rejected with a 400 and the page is not created — re-send the complete document rather than the missing tail. See the [Page Markup Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md) for the full DSL reference. The parser errors are listed under [Common Validation Errors](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md#common-validation-errors).

name.description: Page name of the editable page element.

seo_description.description: Custom meta description for search engine results.

seo_index.description: Whether search engines should index this page. Defaults to false.

seo_title.description: Custom title for search engine results.

show_page_step.description: Optional. Mutates the show_page_step that the page is attached to via the `funnel` block above. Only valid when the page is also being linked to a funnel via the `funnel` block — passing `show_page_step.product_ids` or `show_page_step.bumps` without a funnel link returns 400.

bumps.description: Products to attach to the step as **order bumps** — the optional add-ons offered next to the main products, served to `<checkout/>` and to the SDK as `bumpProducts`. One object per bump, each carrying its own copy. Same additive, all-or-nothing semantics as `product_ids`. A product already attached to the step as a main product is promoted to a bump in place (it keeps its position and its configured variants/prices). A product named in both `product_ids` and `bumps` in the same request is a 400 — a product is either a main product or a bump on a given step, never both. To turn a bump back into a main product, detach it with `DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/products` and re-attach it via `product_ids`.

preheadline.description: Optional short line of copy shown above this bump's offer (for example "One-time offer"). Omit to leave any copy already set on the bump alone. Read it back under `show_page_step.products[].bump_preheadline`.

product_id.description: Public ID of the product to attach as an order bump. Required on every entry; an entry without one is a 400.

product_ids.description: List of product public IDs to append to the step's checkout as regular (main) products. This is **additive** — products are appended to any products already on the step (relevant when `funnel.show_page_step_id` is used to attach to an existing step); products already attached are skipped. All-or-nothing — if any ID does not resolve to a workspace product, the page is not created and a 400 is returned. To remove products, use `DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/products`. See [Manage products on a checkout page](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#manage-products-on-a-checkout-page) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md).

sort_order.description: Optional zero-based position within the funnel when creating with `funnel.funnel_id`. `0` inserts before the first step; omit to append at the end. Ignored when `funnel.show_page_step_id` is provided. Out-of-bounds values return 422.

theme_id.description: The ID of the theme to use for this page.

PageParametersUpdate.description:
Update parameters for a page. Field availability depends on the page type:

**Shared (all page types):** `name`, `description`, `sort_order`, `funnel.show_page_step_id`, `show_page_step.product_ids`, `show_page_step.bumps`.

**Internal (editor) pages only** (returns 422 on external and custom HTML pages): `markup`, `theme_id`, `seo_title`, `seo_description`, `head_code`, `footer_code`, `custom_css`, `live_data_changes`.

**Internal and custom HTML pages** (returns 422 on external pages): `seo_index`, `block_ai_crawler`, `block_ai_search`, `block_ai_assistant`. These act on the page's URL rather than its content (the domain's `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`), so they apply to a custom HTML page too. A custom HTML page's own HTML sets its title and meta tags, which is why `seo_title` and `seo_description` are not accepted there.

**External-only** (returns 422 on other page types): `external_url`.

**Custom HTML pages only** (returns 422 on other page types): `custom_html`. Custom HTML pages also accept `current_path` (like internal pages) — it moves the funnel step's path when the page is a funnel step, or the page's own path when standalone.

The three `block_ai_*` flags are accepted on any internal or custom HTML page. robots.txt expresses the block at every path ClickFunnels serves the page at on its domain: the page's own URL, its funnel step paths, and `/` when it is the site's home page. A page that is only served through another resource's URL (a theme or template page other than the home page, a blog or course page) contributes no rules, so its preference is stored and read back but not enforced. A `200` is therefore not proof that a page is blocked; fetch the domain's `/robots.txt` to confirm. See [Crawler access (AI opt-out)](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#crawler-access-ai-opt-out) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md).

current_path.description: Move the page's URL path (e.g. `/my-page`). Internal and custom HTML pages — returns 422 on external pages. For a custom HTML page that is a funnel step, this moves the STEP's path (the customer-facing URL); when standalone, the page's own path. Returns 422 when the page backs more than one funnel step — the target would be ambiguous.

custom_css.description: Raw CSS to apply at the page level (no <style> wrapper). Maps to the CSS tab in the page editor's Code Editor panel. Internal pages only — returns 422 on external pages. Set to null to clear existing CSS.

custom_css_mode.description: How to handle custom_css. 'append' adds to existing CSS (default), 'replace' overwrites. Internal pages only.

custom_html.description: Replace the entire HTML body of a custom HTML page (max 2MB). An empty or whitespace-only string is rejected with a 422 (omit the field to leave the body unchanged). The stored HTML is served verbatim at the page's URL; the edge cache is purged on write. Custom HTML pages only — returns 422 on other page types. Read the current HTML via `GET /pages/{id}/custom_html`.

description.description: A short description of the page (max 1000 characters).

external_url.description: Update the external URL for an SDK page. External pages only — returns 422 on internal pages. The SDK token is preserved across URL updates. To move external pages to a new origin, see the [Migrate an External Page Domain Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/sdk/migrate-external-page-domain/skill.md#4-patch-one-page-at-a-time).

footer_code.description: Custom code to inject before the closing </body> tag. Internal pages only — returns 422 on external pages. Set to null to clear existing code.

footer_code_mode.description: How to handle footer_code. 'append' adds to existing code (default), 'replace' overwrites. Internal pages only.

funnel.description: Optional funnel mutation block. On update, only `show_page_step_id` is supported — swap the page onto an existing show page step.

show_page_step_id.description: The ID of an existing show page step to attach this page to. The page previously linked to that step becomes an orphan (kept in the workspace, no longer linked to any step). Shared by both internal and external pages.

head_code.description: Custom code to inject into the page's <head> section. Internal pages only — returns 422 on external pages. Set to null to clear existing code.

head_code_mode.description: How to handle head_code. 'append' adds to existing code (default), 'replace' overwrites. Internal pages only.

markup.description: A valid PML (Page Markup Language) string that replaces live visual content; it is not a saved-draft promotion and does not promise deletion of an existing draft blob. PML covers only a subset of what the ClickFunnels page editor can build, so round-tripping an editor page through PML can silently drop content it cannot express. **If the page could have been created or edited in the ClickFunnels editor, stop and get explicit approval from the user before sending this** (a general instruction to update or publish the page does not count): see [the approval guardrail](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md#stop-get-approval-before-overwriting-an-existing-page). Internal pages only — returns 422 on external pages. Markup that stops mid-construct (a tag, attribute value, comment or `<customhtml>` body that never closes, or elements still open at the end of the document) is rejected with a 400 and the page is left untouched — re-send the complete document rather than the missing tail. To add a tracking pixel or other custom code, use `head_code`/`footer_code` instead of rewriting the body; see [Add a tracking pixel or custom code](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#add-a-tracking-pixel-or-custom-code). See the [Page Markup Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md) for the full DSL reference. The parser errors are listed under [Common Validation Errors](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md#common-validation-errors).

Only valid when the page is part of a funnel — passing `show_page_step.product_ids` or `show_page_step.bumps` for a page that isn't linked to a funnel returns 400. Shared by both internal and external pages.

bumps.description: Products to attach to the step as **order bumps** — the optional add-ons offered next to the main products, served to `<checkout/>` and to the SDK as `bumpProducts`. One object per bump, each carrying its own copy. Same additive, all-or-nothing semantics as `product_ids`. A product already attached to the step as a main product is promoted to a bump in place (it keeps its position and its configured variants/prices), which is how you turn an existing attachment into a bump. A product named in both `product_ids` and `bumps` in the same request is a 400 — a product is either a main product or a bump on a given step, never both. To turn a bump back into a main product, detach it with `DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/products` and re-attach it via `product_ids`.

Read it back under `show_page_step.products[].bump_preheadline`.

product_ids.description: List of product public IDs to append to the step's checkout as regular (main) products. This is **additive** — products listed are appended; products already attached are skipped; no products are ever removed via this field, and an existing order bump is never demoted back to a main product by it. All-or-nothing — if any ID does not resolve to a workspace product, no changes are saved and a 400 is returned. To remove products, use `DELETE /api/v2/pages/:id/products`. See [Manage products on a checkout page](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#manage-products-on-a-checkout-page) in the [Pages Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md).

RefineFilterAttributes.description:
A reusable workspace-scoped audience filter composed of one or more criteria joined by a single conjunction.

Public API requests are validated against a [safe-condition whitelist](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#safe-condition-whitelist); criteria outside the whitelist return 422 with a pointer to the developer community.

externalDocs.description: Refine Filters Skill - attributes, clauses, and worked examples

conjunction.description: How the criteria are joined — `and` (all must match) or `or` (any must match).

filter_class.description: The filter class recorded on the saved filter. This API authors `ContactsFilter` and applies `ContactsFilter` and `OrdersFilter`, but the list returns every saved filter in the workspace, and other ClickFunnels surfaces save their own classes here — `ContactsSegmentsFilter`, `ProductsFilter`, `FunnelsFilter` and `ContactUpsellsFilter` all appear in real workspaces. Treat this as an open set: match on the class you want rather than assuming the rest are absent. `null` for a legacy row whose stored state can no longer be decoded (such rows also return empty `criteria`; they can still be deleted).

mixed_conjunctions.description: True when the saved filter joins its conditions with both `and` and `or`, as filters grouped in the UI can. `conjunction` and `criteria` then summarize it as one conjunction over all criteria rather than restating it; request `results` for its exact matches, and do not rebuild it from `criteria`.

name.description: Optional human-readable name for the filter. Must be unique within the workspace when set.

workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace this filter belongs to

RefineFilterAttributes.title: Refine Filter

RefineFilterCriterion.description: A single filter criterion consisting of an attribute, a comparison clause, and a value.

attribute.description:
The contact attribute to filter on (e.g. `tags.id`, `created_at`, `email_address`).
The public API restricts attributes to a [safe whitelist](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#safe-condition-whitelist) — see the [Refine Filters Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md) for the full reference.

clause.description:
The comparison operator for this criterion (e.g. `in`, `eq`, `gte`, `lte`, `st`, `nst`).
Allowed clauses depend on the attribute. Text attributes (`email_address`, `first_name`, `last_name`) only accept `eq` and `sw` on the public API; see the [Refine Filters Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#safe-condition-whitelist).

date_refinement.description: Additional event-date comparison for an attribute that supports date refinement. Preserve this object when reusing a returned criterion; it narrows the audience independently of the selected event IDs.

clause.description: Date comparison operator, such as gte, btwn, or lt.

value.description: ISO8601 date or datetime, two dates for btwn/nbtwn, or days and modifier for relative gt/lt/exct comparisons.

The comparison value. Type depends on the attribute and clause:
- **Option conditions** (tags, products, etc.): a single opaque public id string, or an array of public id strings.
- **Date/datetime conditions**: an ISO 8601 date string (`"2026-01-01"`) or datetime string (`"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"`).
  For `between`/`not_between` clauses supply an array of exactly two date strings.
  For relative `gt`, `lt`, or `exct` clauses supply an object with `days` and a `modifier` of `ago` or `from_now`.
- **Text/numeric conditions**: a plain string or number.
- **Set/not-set clauses**: omit `value` entirely.

`null` when the criterion carries no value, as set/not-set clauses do.

days.description: Number of days used by a relative date clause.

RefineFilterCriterion.title: Refine Filter Criterion

RefineFilterParametersCreate.description:
Parameters for creating a new RefineFilter. The `criteria` array must contain at least one entry.
Each criterion requires `attribute` and `clause`; `value` may be omitted for set/not-set clauses.

### Supported conditions (public API)

The public API restricts criteria to the safe whitelist below. Requests
outside this set return 422 with a pointer to the dev community for
new-condition requests.

| Condition                                                                        | Allowed clauses                                                  | Notes                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `email_address`, `first_name`, `last_name`                                       | `eq`, `sw`                                                        | Text — equals & starts_with only.                                  |
| `anonymous`                                                                      | `eq`, `dne`                                                       | Boolean-style option.                                              |
| `created_at`, `unsubscribed_at`, `last_activity`                                | All standard date clauses                                         | Indexed datetime columns.                                          |
| `tags.id`                                                                        | `eq`, `dne`, `in`, `nin`                                          | Tag membership — must reference workspace-owned tag ids.           |
| `has_affiliate_attribution`, `has_active_affiliate_attribution`, `referred_by_affiliate` | All standard clauses                                  | Affiliate attribution lookups.                                     |
| `email_suppression`                                                              | `st`, `nst`, `eq`, `in`                                           | Email suppression set/not-set or membership.                       |
| `received_broadcast`, `opened_broadcast`, `clicked_broadcast`                   | `eq`, `in`                                                        | **Must include a specific broadcast id.**                          |
| `opted_in_funnel_step`, `opted_in_funnel_at`, `opted_in_on_standalone_page`     | `eq`, `in`                                                        | **Must include a specific funnel/step/page id.**                   |

Conjunction is restricted to `and`. See the full reference at the
[Refine Filters Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#safe-condition-whitelist).

conjunction.description: Join operator for all criteria. Defaults to `and`.

value.description: Comparison value. Relative date clauses use an object with `days` and `modifier`. Omit for set/not-set clauses.

filter_class.description: Filter class. Defaults to `ContactsFilter` (the only supported class).

name.description: Optional human-readable name. Must be unique within the workspace when provided.

RefineFilterParametersCreate.title: Create Refine Filter

RefineFilterParametersUpdate.description:
Parameters for updating an existing RefineFilter. All fields are optional — only provided
fields are updated. When `criteria` is supplied it **replaces** the entire criteria set.

Replacement criteria must satisfy the same safe-condition whitelist enforced on create.
See [Safe condition whitelist](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/refine-filters/skill.md#safe-condition-whitelist) for the full reference.

conjunction.description: Replacement join operator for all criteria.

criteria.description: Replacement criteria array. Must contain at least one entry.

value.description: Comparison value. Relative date clauses use an object with `days` and `modifier`. Omit for set/not-set clauses.

name.description: New name for the filter. Must be unique within the workspace.

SplitTestStepAttributes.description:
A split test step wraps an existing page in a funnel in a two-branch split. Each
variant carries the `show_page_step` + `page` attached to that branch (both `null`
when the branch is empty), plus the branch's traffic `weight` (0..100).

funnel.description: The funnel containing this split test.

variants.description: Ordered variants. Binary split tests always have 2 entries.

page.description: The page attached to this branch, or null if empty.

show_page_step.description: The ShowPageStep function attached to this branch, or null if empty.

weight.description: Percentage of traffic sent to this branch (0..100). Branches must sum to 100.

SplitTestStepAttributes.title: Split Test Step

SplitTestStepParametersCreate.description:
Parameters for wrapping an existing page in a new split test. Provide 1 or 2 variants.
The first variant's `page_id` must already be attached to a step in this funnel's
workflow (that page gets wrapped). The second variant's `page_id` must be a fresh page
(not already used by any step anywhere). No cloning occurs.

### Positioning the split

By default (no `show_page_step_id`), the split lands at the funnel entry —
`sort_order 0` under the workflow root — with all surviving steps moved into a
`Root Step after Sequence End` convergence sequence positioned right after the split.

When `show_page_step_id` references an existing show-page step in this funnel, the
split is inserted **after that step** under the same parent, and steps
N+1...end are migrated under the convergence sequence. This is the "split between
step N and step N+1" shape.

See [Positioning the split](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#positioning-the-split) in the [Funnels Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md) for picking a safe anchor step, and [Placing an external (SDK) page in a branch](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#placing-an-external-sdk-page-in-a-branch) to use a page you host yourself as a variant.

show_page_step_id.description:
Optional. Insert the new split AFTER the workflow step that wraps this
`show_page_step`. Accepts a numeric `Workflows::Steps::ShowPageStep` id
or its obfuscated public id (you can read either off any page response).
When omitted, the split lands at funnel entry.
Caution: creating a split moves the wrapped step inside a branch sequence,
so an id fetched earlier may no longer sit where you think — read the
funnel structure immediately before creating, and note that anchoring on
a step inside another split's branch nests the new split in that branch.

page_id.description: Page ID (required on the first variant; optional on the second).

weight.description: Traffic weight (0..100). Either omit on both variants (defaults 100/0 for 1 variant or 50/50 for 2) or provide on both.

SplitTestStepParametersCreate.title: Create Split Test Step

SplitTestStepParametersUpdate.description:
Parameters for updating a split test's variants. The `variants` array length must
equal the current number of branches (2 for the standard binary case). Each entry may
provide any subset of `{ page_id, weight }`.

page_id.description: New page to attach/swap to this branch. Must be a fresh page (no existing ShowPageStep).

weight.description: Traffic weight (0..100). If any variant provides weight, all must — and they must sum to 100.

SplitTestStepParametersUpdate.title: Update Split Test Step

WebhooksIncomingExternalPurchaseEndpoint.description:
A workspace endpoint that receives purchase events from an external commerce provider.
The `url` is generated by ClickFunnels; configure that URL as the webhook destination in
the provider's own dashboard. Signing secrets are never returned in full by read
operations.

Not every `provider` is available to every workspace: creating an endpoint for one a
workspace has not been granted returns 403.

live_mode.description: Whether the endpoint receives live rather than test purchases. Set only at creation.

provider.description: External commerce provider. The provider cannot be changed after creation.

provider_metadata.description:
Read-only provider-specific state, keyed by provider so the single key both names the
provider and types its value. No provider has fields yet, so every endpoint returns an
empty object under its provider, for example `{"clickbank": {}}` or `{"whop": {}}`.

suppress_order_system_emails.description: Whether ClickFunnels suppresses its order system emails for purchases received by this endpoint.

url.description: Public URL to configure as the provider's incoming webhook destination.

webhook_secret_last_four.description:
Last four characters of the endpoint's signing secret, or null when it has none. Enough
to tell whether a secret is set and whether it matches the one you hold. The full value
is returned only in the create response.

WebhooksIncomingExternalPurchaseEndpoint.title: Incoming External Purchase Endpoint

webhook_secret.description: Signing secret, returned only in this create response and only when ClickFunnels generated it.

created without one and you set it afterwards.

WorkflowStructureAttributes.description:
A complete tree view of a workflow — its header, triggers, and the ordered list
of visible steps. Internal container nodes (sequence steps, end-step markers) are
spliced out. Split steps expose their child branches or variants inline.

Step entries share a common shape (`id`, `public_id`, `step_type`, `name`, `sort_order`,
`state`, `step_type_settings`) and gain type-specific fields:

- **`conditional_split_step`**: `convergence_step_id` + `branches` array (`matched` / `unmatched`), each branch carrying its own `steps`.
- **`split_test_step`**: `convergence_step_id` + `variants` array (each with `weight` and `steps`).
- All other step types: no extra branching fields.

steps.description:
Ordered visible steps. Splits are inlined with their child steps.
Walk this array top-to-bottom to follow the execution order.

convergence_step_id.description: Split steps only. Id of the step where this split's branches reconverge — the first step that runs after the split, which every branch continues to. Example: a conditional_split_step (id 203) whose matched/unmatched branches both lead to the same next step (id 206) → convergence_step_id: 206. null when nothing follows the split (it ends the flow). The referenced step always appears in this tree.

sort_order.description: Position within its own container — not globally unique across the tree.

step_type_settings.description: One-key map whose key is the step type. See Workflows::Step for the per-type shape.

triggers.description: Active triggers attached to the workflow (summary shape).

WorkflowsRunAttributes.description:
An execution record tracking a contact's progress through a workflow.

`status` is derived:
- `canceled` — the run was explicitly canceled.
- `completed` — the run finished normally.
- `paused` — the unfinished run has been explicitly paused.
- `active` — none of the above; currently in-progress.

The list endpoint returns only standard automation runs (`type: null`);
survey/STI run subtypes are excluded.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the run completed. Null if still in progress.

contact.description: Compact enrolled contact, or null when missing, deleted, or unavailable in this workflow's workspace. The original contact_id is retained.

contact_id.description: Raw integer ID of the enrolled contact

current_step_id.description: Raw integer ID of the step the run is currently at. Null when not at a step.

event_id.description: Raw integer ID of the triggering event that started this run, if any.

paused_at.description: Timestamp when the run was last paused. Null if never paused.

skip_communication.description: When true, communication steps (send email, etc.) are skipped for this run.

status.description: Derived execution status.

type.description: STI type column. Always `null` for standard automation runs (the only subtype the list endpoint returns).

updated_at.description: Last run update time, not the time the contact entered the current step.

workflow_id.description: Integer ID of the parent workflow

Parameters for manually enrolling a contact into a workflow. The workflow
must be enabled (status `live`) — otherwise returns 422.

skip_communication.description: When true, communication steps (send email, chat message, etc.) are skipped for this run. Defaults to false.

WorkflowsStepAttributes.description:
A single action or split step within a workflow.

`step_type` equals the single key inside `step_type_settings` and identifies which
step class this is. The full list of step types, the per-type settings each one
carries, the write-only `send_email_step` inline-body fields, and how FK ids are
serialized are all documented on the **`step_type_settings`** field below — that
field is the single canonical reference, and the Create Step / Update Step request
bodies point to it.

`parent_step_id` and `branch` report where a step sits when it lives inside a split
branch; see the Create Step / Update Step schemas for setting placement on write.

branch.description: For conditional splits — `matched` or `unmatched`. For split tests — the 0-based variant index as a string. Null for trunk steps.

convergence_step_id.description: Id of the step a split's branches reconverge at — the first step that runs after the split, which every branch continues to. Example: a conditional_split_step (id 203) whose matched/unmatched branches both lead to the same next step (id 206) → convergence_step_id 206. It is null in two cases: a split that ends the flow (nothing follows it), and any non-split step (the field only applies to conditional_split_step / split_test_step). Use step_type to tell them apart — a null on a non-split step just means the field does not apply. When non-null, the referenced step always appears in this response.

parent_step_id.description: Raw integer id of the parent split step when this step lives inside a branch. Null for trunk steps.

sort_order.description: Zero-based position **within this step's own container** (the trunk, or a split's branch/convergence sequence). It is therefore **container-local, not globally unique** — it restarts at 0 for steps after a split. In `/structure`, follow the `steps` array order for execution flow, not `sort_order`.

step_type.description: The step class key (same as the single key in `step_type_settings`).

step_type_settings.description:
A single-key map: the one key is the step type (identical to `step_type`) and its
value carries that type's settings. **This is the canonical reference for step
settings — the Create Step and Update Step request bodies point here.**

Available types —

**Action steps** (non-branching):
`send_email_step`, `send_asset_step`, `send_chat_message_step`, `contact_tag_step`,
`contact_custom_attribute_step`, `delay_step`, `notify_step`, `deliver_webhook_step`,
`enroll_step`, `unenroll_contact_step`, `grant_community_access_step`,
`revoke_community_access_step`, `create_opportunity_step`, `move_step`

**Split steps** (branching): `conditional_split_step`, `split_test_step`

### Per-type fields

- `send_email_step`: `subject`, `preheadline`, `template_id`, `from_address_id`, `reply_to_address_id`, plus write-only `html_body`/`text_body` (see "send_email_step inline body" below)
- `send_asset_step`: `asset_id`
- `send_chat_message_step`: `inbox_key`, `message`, `subject`, `start_new_conversation`
- `contact_tag_step`: `action` (`"Add Tags"` or `"Remove Tags"`), `contacts_tag_ids` (array of raw integer tag ids)
- `contact_custom_attribute_step`: `action`, `value`, `field_id` (a Forms::Field id — discoverable via the Forms API)
- `delay_step`: `delay_type` (`relative`/`day_of_week`/`day_of_month`/`specific_date`), `duration`, `interval`, `time_zone`, `use_contact_time_zone`, `use_execution_window`, `day_of_week`, `date_of_month`, `specific_date`, `past_date_action`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `execution_window_days`. For `specific_date`, send `specific_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, no more than a year away) and `start_time` (`HH:MM`, 24-hour), read in `time_zone` (or each contact's own zone with `use_contact_time_zone: true`). A moment that has already passed is accepted. `past_date_action` (`continue`, the default, `end` or `skip_to_next_delay`) decides what happens to a contact who reaches the step after that moment: continue to the next step right away, end their run, or move straight to the next wait step on their path (a delay, pause or countdown event delay) without running the steps in between, ending their run if there is none. `time_zone` is a human-readable time zone name — the label shown in the builder's dropdown, e.g. `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`, `London`, `Tokyo`. A TZ database id is also accepted and is stored as the name that keeps the same clock (`America/New_York` and `America/Toronto` → `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`, `Europe/London` → `London`), so the response echoes the name, not the id you sent. Any other value is rejected 422. The full list of names and how they map to TZ ids is in [our Time Zones guide](https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/timezones). Set `use_contact_time_zone: true` to use each contact's own zone instead.
- `notify_step`: `message`, `notify_type` (array), `user_ids` (array of user ids — must be team members; discover via `GET /teams/{team_id}/memberships` → `user_id`. A non-member id is rejected 422.)
- `deliver_webhook_step`: `webhooks_outgoing_endpoint_id`
- `enroll_step`: `course_ids` (array), `section_ids` (array). **Enrollment happens per `section_ids`** — provide the section ids to enroll in (discover via `GET /api/v2/courses/{course_id}/sections`). `course_ids` alone is accepted and the step reads `active`, but enrolls nothing at run time.
- `unenroll_contact_step`: `course_ids` (array), `section_ids` (array). Unenroll honors both `course_ids` and `section_ids`.
- `grant_community_access_step`: `space_ids` (array)
- `revoke_community_access_step`: `space_ids` (array)
- `create_opportunity_step`: `name`, `value`, `assignment_strategy` (`unassigned`/`membership`/`pipeline`/`round_robin`; any other value is rejected 422), `move_existing`, `sales_pipelines_stage_id`, `sales_pipeline_id`, `membership_id`, `membership_ids` (array)
- `move_step`: `workflow_id`
- `conditional_split_step`: `condition` object with `filter_id` (raw integer RefineFilter id on read; integer id or public_id on write) and `is_setup` boolean
- `split_test_step`: `variants` array, each with `weight` (0..100, two entries summing to 100)

### `send_email_step` — template & inline body

A `send_email_step` always owns its email. On **create**, a provided `template_id`
is **copied** into a fresh step-owned template (it is never a live reference to the
original), and an inline `html_body`/`text_body` instead mints a new step-owned
template. This deliberately mirrors the builder UI, which always makes its own copy
so edits to a step's email never touch the source. `template_id` takes precedence
when both a `template_id` and an inline body are supplied. The create response's
`step_type_settings.send_email_step.template_id` is the step-owned copy's id, not
the source template's id.

Because the step owns its template, `template_id` is **create-only and cannot be
changed on update** — a `PATCH` that includes `template_id` returns `422`. To change
an existing step's email, edit it **in place** by sending `html_body`/`text_body`
(this patches the step's own template — no new template is created); to use a
different template, create a new step. `html_body`/`text_body` are write-only and are
never returned in `step_type_settings`. For
`from_address_id`/`reply_to_address_id`, pick an address whose top-level
`usable_as_sender` is true, not one whose sending domain is merely `verified`.
See [Inline body on a workflow send-email step](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/emails/skill.md#inline-body-on-a-workflow-send-email-step) in the [Emails Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/emails/skill.md).

### FK id serialization

Response FK values (`*_id`, `*_ids`) are serialized as **raw integers**. On write,
those same FK fields accept either integer ids or obfuscated public_ids in the same
workspace/team scope.

workflow_id.description: Integer ID of the parent workflow

WorkflowsStepAttributes.title: Workflows::Step

WorkflowsStepParametersCreate.description:
Parameters for adding a new step to a workflow. `step_type_settings` must contain
exactly one key naming the step type.

### Placement

- **Trunk (default)**: omit `parent_step_id` and `branch` to append at the end of the main sequence.
- **Inside a split branch**: set `parent_step_id` to the id (integer or public_id) of the split step, and `branch` to:
  - `matched` or `unmatched` for a `conditional_split_step` (the legacy `match`/`fallback` aliases are still accepted)
  - A 0-based variant index string (`"0"`, `"1"`) for a `split_test_step`
- **Specific position**: use `position` (0-based integer) or `after_step_id` (id of the preceding step).

See [Branching](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/workflows/skill.md#branching) in the [Workflows Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/workflows/skill.md) for where a step with no placement lands relative to a split.

For `split_test_step`, the `variants` array must have exactly 2 entries with integer weights summing to 100.
For `conditional_split_step`, provide `condition.filter_id` (integer id or obfuscated RefineFilter public_id).

Creating a `send_email_step` requires a complete business mailing address in
the workspace's email settings. Configure it with
`PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id}/emails/settings`; otherwise creation returns `422`.

after_step_id.description: Step id or public_id of the step to insert after. Mutually exclusive with `position`.

branch.description: Branch selector — `matched`/`unmatched` for conditional splits (legacy `match`/`fallback` still accepted); `"0"`/`"1"` for split tests.

name.description: Optional human-readable name. Defaults to a titleized version of the step type.

parent_step_id.description: Step id or public_id of a split step. Required when placing a step inside a branch.

position.description: 0-based position within the container. Mutually exclusive with `after_step_id`.

step_type_settings.description:
Exactly one key naming the step type, with its settings as the value. On a
`send_email_step` a `template_id` is copied into a new step-owned template, and
you may instead pass the write-only `html_body`/`text_body` to author one inline.

**See the `step_type_settings` field on the Workflows::Step response schema
(`#/components/schemas/WorkflowsStepAttributes`) for the full per-type field
catalog, the `send_email_step` inline-body rules, and FK id handling.**

WorkflowsStepParametersCreate.title: Create Workflows::Step

WorkflowsStepParametersUpdate.description:
Parameters for updating an existing step. Only `step_type_settings`,
`name`, and placement fields (`parent_step_id`, `branch`, `position`,
`after_step_id`) are accepted. All are optional.

Moving split steps is not supported and returns 422.

parent_step_id.description: Move this step into a split branch (sets new container).

step_type_settings.description:
One-key settings map; the key must match the step's existing type.

A `send_email_step` update **cannot change `template_id`** (it is create-only —
including it returns `422`); edit the email in place with `html_body`/`text_body`
instead, or create a new step to use a different template.

**See the `step_type_settings` field on the Workflows::Step response schema
(`#/components/schemas/WorkflowsStepAttributes`) for the full per-type field
catalog, the `send_email_step` inline-body rules, and FK id handling.**

WorkflowsStepStatsAttributes.description: Stats for one workflow step over the requested timerange. Every step type reports `contacts`; only a `send_email_step` reports `email`, which is `null` for every other step type. Counts are unique contacts unless noted; rates are whole percentages; money is a decimal string in `currency`.

contacts.description: Where contacts stand in relation to this step. Every step type reports these; they are the two numbers the workflow builder shows under each step.

are_here.description: Contacts at this step right now — runs whose current step is this one. A live count; it does not follow `timerange`.

were_here.description: Contacts who left this step inside the window, counting a contact once per pass through it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary values (e.g. USD, EUR). `email.revenue` counts only orders paid in this currency. `null` when the workspace has no currency set, in which case there is nothing to filter on and revenue sums every currency its orders were paid in.

email.description: Engagement and attributed revenue for the email this step sends. `null` for every step type except `send_email_step` — a step that sends nothing has nothing to report, which is not the same as performing badly.

performance.description: Engagement inside the window. Rates are rounded to whole percentages, so a share under 0.5% reads 0 next to a non-zero count; the counts are authoritative. Numerator and denominator are each counted inside the window on their own, so a rate is not a share of one fixed group of contacts — see `open_rate`. These counts include test-mode sends, while `revenue` counts live-mode orders only, so the revenue-per-X figures divide live-only money by counts that may include test traffic.

bounce_rate.description: Bounces as a whole percentage of `recipients`; 0 when `recipients` is 0.

click_rate.description: Unique clicks as a whole percentage of `recipients`. Counted the same way as `open_rate`, so it can exceed 100 and is 0 when `recipients` is 0.

click_to_open_rate.description: Unique clicks as a whole percentage of unique opens; 0 when there are no opens.

clicked.description: Total clicks inside the window, counting repeat clicks by the same contact

failed.description: Contacts whose send failed, either refused outright or timed out in the queue. A contact that failed both ways counts once.

open_rate.description: Unique opens as a whole percentage of `recipients`. Both are counted inside the window on their own, so an open of an email sent before the window counts while its send does not; the figure can exceed 100 when few new sends meet many opens of older emails, and it is 0 whenever `recipients` is 0. Widen the window to cover the sends you care about.

opened.description: Total opens inside the window, counting repeat opens by the same contact

recipients.description: Distinct contacts the step sent to inside the window, including any reached in test mode. Every rate below except `click_to_open_rate` is a share of this, not of `sends`.

sends.description: Emails this step sent inside the window, counting a contact once per pass through the step. A workflow that loops, or a contact re-entered into it, makes this larger than `recipients`.

spam_complaints.description: Contacts who reported this email as spam

unique_clicks.description: Contacts who clicked at least once inside the window

unique_opens.description: Contacts who opened at least once inside the window

unsubscribe_rate.description: Unsubscribes as a whole percentage of `recipients`; 0 when `recipients` is 0.

unsubscribed.description: Contacts who unsubscribed from this email

revenue.description: Orders attributed to this step's email: the buyer's last tracked source within 30 days was a click on one of its links, so a later touch from elsewhere supersedes it. Each order contributes its FIRST paid invoice, and only when that invoice was issued inside the window - renewals never count, and an order whose first payment predates the window contributes nothing even if a renewal was paid inside it. Only live-mode orders paid in the workspace `currency` are counted.

orders_count.description: Attributed orders whose FIRST paid invoice was issued inside the window

per_recipient.description: Revenue divided by `recipients`, as a decimal string in `currency`

per_unique_click.description: Revenue divided by unique clicks, as a decimal string in `currency`

per_unique_open.description: Revenue divided by unique opens, as a decimal string in `currency`

total.description: Revenue attributed to the step, as a decimal string in `currency`

step.description: The workflow step these stats belong to

step_type.description: The step's type, e.g. `send_email_step` or `delay_step`. `email` is `null` unless this is `send_email_step`.

timerange.description: The window the stats cover, after clamping. Read it back rather than assuming the window you asked for was used. Every number follows it except `contacts.are_here`, which is a live count.

workflow.description: The workflow the step belongs to

WorkflowsStepStatsAttributes.title: Workflow Step Stats

WorkflowsTriggerAttributes.description:
A trigger attached to a workflow. Each trigger has an `event_type_key` (e.g.
`$contact.tag_applied`) and optional condition FK ids that narrow when the
trigger fires. An invalid `event_type_key` returns 422. NOTE: for page events
(`$optin`, `$view`), `funnel_id` matches every page in that funnel and `page_id`
narrows to one page. Website pages outside a funnel carry no funnel, so scope
those by `page_id` only. A condition FK that
is `null` matches every value, so read these fields back to confirm a
trigger's scope.

active.description: Whether the trigger is active and will enroll contacts.

allow_anonymous_contacts.description: Whether the trigger fires for anonymous (non-identified) contacts.

appointments_calendar_id.description: Raw integer Appointments::Calendar id used as a condition filter.

appointments_event_type_id.description: Raw integer Appointments::EventType id used as a condition filter.

calendar_event_id.description: Raw integer CalendarEvent id used as a condition filter.

cancellation_product_id.description: Raw integer Product id for cancellation condition filtering.

cancellation_product_variant_id.description: Raw integer Products::Variant id for cancellation condition filtering.

communities_space_group_id.description: Raw integer Communities::SpaceGroup id used as a condition filter.

communities_space_id.description: Raw integer Communities::Space id used as a condition filter.

community_id.description: Raw integer Community id used as a condition filter.

contacts_tag_id.description: Raw integer Contacts::Tag id used as a condition filter.

course_id.description: Raw integer Course id used as a condition filter.

courses_lesson_id.description: Raw integer Courses::Lesson id used as a condition filter.

courses_section_id.description: Raw integer Courses::Section id used as a condition filter.

current_sales_pipelines_stage_id.description: Raw integer Sales::Pipelines::Stage id used as a condition filter.

emails_broadcasts_id.description: Raw integer Emails::Broadcast id used as a condition filter.

event_type_key.description: The event that fires this trigger (e.g. `$contact.tag_applied`, `$order.successful_purchase`).

event_type_name.description: Human-readable name of the event type.

funnel_id.description: Raw integer Funnel id used as a condition filter.

page_id.description: Raw integer Page id used as a condition filter.

product_id.description: Raw integer Product id used as a condition filter.

product_variant_id.description: Raw integer Products::Variant id used as a condition filter.

sales_pipelines_id.description: Raw integer Sales::Pipeline id used as a condition filter.

subscription_cancelation_reason.description: Only set on `$order.cancelled` (subscription cancellation) triggers — the cancellation-reason token the contact selected (e.g. `too_expensive`). `null` for every other event type.

subscription_variant_to_id.description: Raw integer Products::Variant id for subscription upgrade/downgrade triggers.

BearerAuth.description:
A workspace API key or an OAuth access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Both carry the same scope vocabulary as the `OAuth2` scheme below. Category-only
scopes restrict access to the categories they name. Coarse wildcards remain additive:
`read contacts:read` reads every category, while `write contacts:read` can write every
category. Omit coarse scopes when restricting access to specific categories.
Legacy tokens with only coarse scopes retain their existing unrestricted access;
a bare `read` scope alone does not enforce read-only access.

OAuth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for REST integrations. Create a Platform Application
and follow `https://developers.myclickfunnels.com/docs/oauth-20` to connect users.
Authorization server metadata is published at
`https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
Dynamic client registration at `/oauth/register` is for MCP clients only; MCP-scoped
tokens must use `https://agents.myclickfunnels.com/mcp`, not the REST API.

Scopes are least-privilege by category. Ask for the two coarse wildcards (`read`,
`write`) only when an integration genuinely needs the whole workspace; otherwise ask
for the `<category>:read` / `<category>:write` pairs you use. `write` implies `read`
for the same category. Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) for this API lives at
`https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

scopes.read: Read any resource in the granted workspaces
scopes.write: Read and write any resource in the granted workspaces

info.description:
The ClickFunnels REST API that powers webhooks, native integrations, and Zapier lets you manage your ClickFunnels data, automate your workflows, and recreate ClickFunnels functionality in your own apps.

### For AI agents

This document is the catalogue: every operation ClickFunnels exposes over REST is described here, with a unique operationId, typed schemas, and the scopes it needs. It is served from `/openapi.json`, `/openapi.yaml`, `/api/openapi.{json,yaml}`, and `/api/v2/openapi.{json,yaml}` on the accounts host.

Three things it does not describe, each one request away:

- [MCP server](https://agents.myclickfunnels.com/mcp): the app-native Model Context Protocol server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE). Prefer it over raw REST when your client supports MCP - it describes itself at runtime.
- [Skill guides](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/skill.md), also as an [Agent Skills index](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): one task guide per job (pages, blogs, products, orders, workflows, emails, courses, stats, external SDK pages). Read the guide that matches your job before your first write. [llms.txt](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/llms.txt) covers when to use ClickFunnels at all, how to get credentials, and how to behave around rate limits.
- [Protected resource metadata](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource) (RFC 9728) and [authorization server metadata](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) (RFC 8414): the scope vocabulary and the OAuth endpoints. Dynamic client registration is for MCP clients only.

On ClickFunnels-owned API hosts (`myclickfunnels.com` and its subdomains), the OpenAPI specification responses and API authentication failures (401, or 403 for insufficient scope) carry those links in an RFC 8288 `Link` header, so clients can discover the documentation and authentication metadata from those responses. Requests sent through a customer's custom domain keep the Bearer challenge but omit those discovery pointers.

patch.description:
Update a blog post.

Pass `markup` to update the post's visual content via PML. It replaces the whole body, and PML covers only a subset of what the ClickFunnels editor can build, so if this post could have been written or edited in the editor, stop and get explicit approval from the user first: see [the approval guardrail](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/page-markup/skill.md#stop-get-approval-before-overwriting-an-existing-page). Omit `markup` to change only metadata. Invalid markup returns 400 and neither the post metadata nor the markup is saved. Pass `expand[]=markup` to have the markup returned in the response.

See [Updating a blog post](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/blogs/skill.md#updating-a-blog-post) in the [Blogs Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/blogs/skill.md). To publish a draft, see [Publish separately](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/blogs/import-external-post/skill.md#7-publish-separately) and [Two gotchas worth knowing](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/blogs/skill.md#two-gotchas-worth-knowing).

get.description:
Fetches a previously saved contact filter by id. This route is shallow — the workspace is resolved from
the filter itself, so no `workspace_id` is required in the path. Use the `id` (or `public_id`) returned by
`POST /api/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}/contacts/filters` with `save: true`.

Returns the same resource shape as the generate endpoint, with the identity fields populated. The
`stable_id` is re-derived from the saved filter. To apply it on the contacts index, keep it opaque and
let the HTTP client encode the complete `stable_id` query parameter value; with curl, use
`-G --data-urlencode "stable_id=$STABLE_ID"`.

parameters.description: The saved filter's `id` or `public_id`.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Return projected matches inline. Pass `true` for ids only; omit for the filter definition alone.
parameters.name: results

count.description: Include the bounded total count. May require another filter evaluation.

fields.description: Comma-separated fields to project. Defaults to `id`.

max_bytes.description: Caller-set row byte budget. Defaults to 3072 and is capped at 4194304.

conjunction.description: How the criteria are joined — `and` (all must match) or `or` (any must match).

name.description: Name of the saved filter, or `null` when it has no name.

stable_id.description: URL-encoded Refine `stable_id` token in the standard gzip+base64 full-state format — interoperable with the server-rendered filter UI. To apply it on the contacts index, keep it opaque and let the HTTP client encode the complete `stable_id` query parameter value (with curl, use `-G --data-urlencode "stable_id=$STABLE_ID"`).

post.description:
Publish one or more course sections AND the lessons they contain. Provide exactly one of `target_ids` (a nonempty array of course-section public IDs) or `target_all: true` to publish every unpublished non-root section of the course. Explicit target IDs must identify sections in this course. Targeting the root "Primary module" container (or using `target_all`) expands to every unpublished non-root section. A missing or empty `courses_sections_publish_action` wrapper is a malformed request and returns `400`; a well-formed wrapper with a missing or conflicting selection, or an invalid/cross-course target ID, returns `422`. If a root or `target_all` request has no unpublished content to publish, the response is `200 OK` with a message (not an error).
The action runs asynchronously — poll with `GET /api/v2/courses/sections/publish_actions/{id}`. The `status` field is `queued`, `scheduled`, or `processing` while work remains and `completed` when it is done. Compare `performed_count` to `target_count` for section progress. `published_lessons_count` reports lesson publish states this action changed, excluding lessons already live.
Set `auto_enroll: true` to grant existing course enrollees access to the newly published sections. Pair with `send_email: true` to notify them.
Use `scheduled_for` (ISO 8601, must be a future datetime) to defer the publish.
See [Publishing](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/courses/skill.md#publishing) in the [Courses Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/courses/skill.md) for when this bulk action is the right choice.

post.description:
Makes the course live by setting `published_at`. Pass an optional future `published_at` to schedule the publish; omit it (or leave it blank) to publish immediately. A `published_at` in the past is rejected.
By default this publishes only the course record. To publish a brand-new course in one step, pass `publish_sections_and_lessons: true`. Before the `200 OK` response, the requested publish timestamp is set on the course, every eligible unpublished non-root section, and all unpublished or scheduled lessons underneath it. Drip and blocked section gates remain in effect. Section publish actions may still perform follow-up work asynchronously, and each records how many lessons it published in `published_lessons_count`. Otherwise sections and lessons stay draft until published via the `Courses::Sections::PublishAction` resource.
Returns 422 if `published_at` is supplied but is not a valid ISO 8601 datetime, or if it is in the past.
See [Publishing](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/courses/skill.md#publishing) in the [Courses Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/courses/skill.md) for the publish paths.

publish_sections_and_lessons.description: When `true`, sets the requested publish timestamp on the course, every eligible unpublished non-root section, and all unpublished or scheduled lessons before returning the response. Drip and blocked section gates remain in effect. Section publish actions may continue follow-up processing asynchronously. Use this for a one-step publish of a new course. Defaults to `false`.

published_at.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime at which the course should become live. Must be now or in the future — a past datetime is rejected with a 422. Omit or leave blank to publish immediately.

post.description:
Send (or schedule) an email broadcast by creating a Send Action. This is the same trigger the ClickFunnels dashboard fires when you click "Send".
The request body is optional — a bodyless POST dispatches the broadcast immediately. Pass a future `send_at` inside `emails_broadcasts_send_action` to schedule the broadcast for that moment (to the minute), converted into the broadcast's time zone. A `send_at` in the past returns 422.
The broadcast must be ready to send before this call will succeed. It requires: - A topic assigned (`topic_ids` is non-empty) - A from-address with `usable_as_sender: true` - A complete workspace marketing address (set via the Email Settings endpoint)
If any of these conditions are not met, the endpoint returns 422 with a message listing what is missing.
The send runs asynchronously. The returned Send Action record tracks progress: poll `GET /api/v2/emails/broadcasts/send_actions/{id}` and compare `performed_count` to `target_count`.
See [Sending or scheduling a broadcast](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/emails/skill.md#sending-or-scheduling-a-broadcast) in the [Emails Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/emails/skill.md).

get.description:
The HTML an email broadcast actually sent, one entry per distinct document.

A broadcast points at its template rather than copying it, so the template's body
(`GET /api/v2/emails/templates/{id}?expand[]=html_body`) shows the template as it is now and
changes if the template is edited after the send. This endpoint returns what recipients
received, as recorded when each send went out: the template plus the preview text,
mailing address and branding the workspace adds, before merge tags were filled in and links
were rewritten per contact. No contact data is included.

A split-test broadcast returns one version per variant whose preview text differs. Variants
that differ only in subject share a document, because the subject is not part of it. Match a
version to the broadcast's `variants` (`GET /api/v2/emails/broadcasts/{id}`) by
`preheadline`. A broadcast whose template or workspace settings changed while it was sending
returns a version for each document it sent.

Broadcasts that sent before documents were recorded (about mid-2023), and broadcasts that
have not sent, return an empty `versions` list.

Three ideas for this week

The one idea that matters this week

get.description:
Delivery progress, engagement and revenue for one email broadcast, the same numbers as
the broadcast's page in the ClickFunnels dashboard.

The numbers cover the broadcast's send window, returned as `timerange`: from when
sending began until two weeks after it completed, or until now while it has not
completed, capped at 90 days after sending began. A broadcast that has not started
sending reports the last 90 days, with every number zero. There are no timerange parameters;
the `timerange_start` and `timerange_end` parameters of the funnel and page stats
endpoints are refused with a 422 rather than silently ignored.

Counts are unique contacts, except `opened` and `clicked`, which count every event.
Rates are whole percentages (0-100) of the audience (`progress.total`), rounded to the
nearest integer, so a share under 0.5% reads 0 next to a non-zero count; the counts are
authoritative. `click_to_open_rate` is unique clicks over unique opens. Revenue is
attributed to the broadcast when the buyer reached the order through one of its links,
summed across every send of the broadcast. Only live-mode transactions in the workspace
currency are counted (a workspace with no currency set has nothing to filter on, so
`currency` is `null` and every currency is summed); test-mode orders are excluded.

`progress.total` is the audience size recorded when the broadcast sent, summed over every
send of the broadcast, and is `null` before the first send has run. Stats are cached for a
few minutes while a broadcast is sending and longer once it has completed.

The split-test variants and the winner are on the broadcast record itself
(`GET /api/v2/emails/broadcasts/{id}`). Add `expand[]=variants` for each variant's numbers:
recipients, bounces, unique clicks, unsubscribes and spam complaints, reported separately for
the split test and for the winner's send to the rest of the audience, so variants are
compared on the test alone. Only the open pixel identifies a variant, so these are derived
from the record of which contacts were sent which variant. That record is removed 30 days
after the broadcast completes, and from then on `test` and `winner_send` are `null`; read
them once the two-week stats window has closed and within 30 days of completion. Expanding variants can take a
few seconds on a large broadcast the first time; the result is cached like the other numbers.

post.description: Create an independent editable draft from a broadcast that has been complete for at least 24 hours, including the exact 24-hour boundary. Copies published content, sender and reply-to settings, topics, and A/B variants and settings; clears the old schedule and results. The audience is contacts recorded as sent the source without a recorded open, subject to current subscription and suppression rules. It is evaluated when the separate send flow prepares recipients; a later open does not remove a queued recipient. This request never sends or schedules the draft. Review or edit the returned broadcast, then create its send action separately. Takes no body or content overrides. Each successful call creates another draft, so retrying is not idempotent. Requires email write access, source read access, permission to create broadcasts, and a workspace grant covering the source workspace.

get.description: Retrieve a single email sending domain (DKIM/SPF/DMARC), including its ownership, transport, readiness, and return-path flags plus the DNS records to add at the provider. These are **email sending** domains - for website/hosting domains, see **listDomains**. `verified` reports transport only; `ready_for_sending` requires both workspace ownership and transport, while return-path verification is independent. Ownership is confirmed by connecting the domain, as `www.example.com` or another subdomain of it, to this workspace as a website/hosting domain in the ClickFunnels app, not through this API. `dkim_record` is `null` until the DKIM key finishes generating - re-POST the same name to **createEmailsDomains** to retry provisioning. This read returns the stored DNS verification state and never triggers a live DNS lookup (use `verifyEmailsDomains` to re-check), while `ownership_verified` is always current.

example.name: example.com
next_steps: Connect example.com to this workspace in ClickFunnels so ownership is confirmed. Addresses on this domain cannot send until it is, even once every record below verifies.
Add dkim_record, spf_record, and dmarc_record at the DNS provider for example.com to authenticate email transport.
Recommended for ClickFunnels bounce handling: add return_address_record at the DNS provider.
DNS changes can take up to 48 hours to propagate. Re-check with POST /api/v2/emails/domains/QrStUv/verify; results are cached for about 10 minutes.
Manual setup help: https://support.myclickfunnels.com/docs/email-settings-how-to-verify-email-dns-records

post.description: Re-run the DNS checks for DKIM, SPF, DMARC, and the return path, cached for about 10 minutes, and return the refreshed status together with the current ownership state. A `200` means the check ran, not that it passed, so always read the booleans back. `verified` reports transport only and becomes true when DKIM, SPF, and DMARC are all live, or when a verified SMTP setting exists. `ownership_verified` reports workspace control of the name, which comes from connecting the domain, as `www.example.com` or another subdomain of it, to this workspace as a website/hosting domain in the ClickFunnels app rather than from any API call. `ready_for_sending` becomes true only when both are true. Return-path verification is checked but remains independent and is not required for readiness. DNS changes can take up to 48 hours to propagate.

post.description:
Create a durable asynchronous receipt for a new same-workspace copy of the source funnel. Send no request body. Every accepted request creates a distinct copy; polling or retry delivery of the same action never creates another copy.

The copy keeps the source site and domain, receives a localized generated name and path, starts in test mode with its workflow disabled, and has independent pages and steps. Product and automation links are retained. Tags, history, and share links are not copied. Funnels with external SDK pages cannot be duplicated.

Poll `GET /funnels/clone_actions/{id}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`, then fetch `cloned_funnel_id` with the Fetch Funnel endpoint.

delete.description:
Remove a conditional split from the funnel.

**A 1-branch conditional split is not a supported state**, so any value
of `branch` collapses the entire split:

- `DELETE /funnels/{funnel_id}/conditional_split_steps/{id}` (default
  `branch=both`) → removes the entire conditional split, both branches
  discarded.
- `DELETE /funnels/{funnel_id}/conditional_split_steps/{id}?branch=matched`
  → removes the entire conditional split; the **unmatched** branch's
  pages are promoted up under the split's parent so they remain
  attached to the funnel's main workflow.
- `DELETE /funnels/{funnel_id}/conditional_split_steps/{id}?branch=unmatched`
  → removes the entire conditional split; the **matched** branch's
  pages are promoted up under the split's parent.

See [Destroying a conditional split](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md#destroying-a-conditional-split) in the [Funnels Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md) for how the collapse fits into the rest of the conditional-split surface.

parameters.description: Optional branch to remove. One of `matched`, `unmatched`, or `both` (default).
parameters.name: branch

patch.description:
Update a split test's variants: attach a page to an empty branch, swap an existing
variant's page, or adjust the weights. The `variants` array length must equal the
number of branches in the split test (2 for the standard binary case).

- Weight rules: if *any* variant provides `weight`, all variants must provide it and
  the values must be integers 0..100 summing to 100. If *none* provide weight, weights
  stay unchanged.
- Page-id rules per variant:
  - Equal to current `page_id` → no-op.
  - Branch currently empty + new `page_id` provided → attach.
  - Branch currently has a page + new different `page_id` → swap (old step destroyed).
  - `page_id: null` or blank is rejected (detach is out of scope — use DELETE with
    `branch` parameter instead).
- Any page being attached/swapped-in must: (a) be in the same workspace, (b) be a
  `user_page`, and (c) have no existing `ShowPageStep` anywhere in any funnel.

get.description:
Retrieve detailed statistics for a funnel, including a summary of key metrics
and optional per-step breakdowns of views, opt-ins, sales, and earnings.

Defaults to a 30-day timerange ending now. Override with `timerange_start` and
`timerange_end`. Timerange values are automatically clamped: future end dates
are clamped to now, windows exceeding 90 days are clamped to 90 days, and if
start is after end the window resets to 30 days ending at `timerange_end`.

By default the response includes a `page_public_ids` array. Use
`expand[]=steps` to receive a `steps` array with per-step metrics instead.

The metric names in the response are defined in [Metric vocabulary](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/stats/skill.md#metric-vocabulary) in the [Stats Skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/stats/skill.md), which also walks a [recurring funnel auditor agent](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/stats/skill.md#example-use-case---recurring-funnel-auditor-agent) built on this endpoint.

delete.description:
Permanently remove an active or archived, unshared funnel only when its workflow has no steps beyond its generated root. Populated funnels must be archived instead. The workflow and its root step are retained.

An otherwise empty funnel can still be referenced by products, affiliate campaigns, or store upsells. If a database foreign key blocks deletion, the endpoint returns 409 with guidance to archive instead; the funnel and its dependent records are preserved.

Funnels write access is required. If the funnel has attached workflow triggers, deletion also requires Workflows write access because those triggers are deleted with the funnel. Trigger-free funnels require only Funnels write access.

put.description:
Update a funnel's settings, including its path, favicon, domain, and tags, by numeric id or public id with the `funnel` JSON root. PATCH is also supported. The favicon is writable only on this operation; creation already accepts a path. The target image, domain, and tags must belong to the funnel's workspace. A path edit cannot take an occupied or historical URL or move the root path. Domain changes can continue propagating after this response.

`live_mode` controls test versus live payment processing; changing it does not publish page content. Use `PUT /api/v2/pages/:id` or `PATCH /api/v2/pages/:id` for an intentional live page content replacement and `GET /api/v2/pages/:id` to read the resource back. There is currently no atomic whole-funnel release or pollable publish receipt.

Boolean `true`/`false` and their string forms assign `live_mode`; null, empty and other values leave it unchanged. Set it to true only when live payment processing is intended.

Use head_code and footer_code to inject custom code. Their modes default to append; use replace for repeatable writes. Null clears code.

get.description:
A funnel's steps as a single, flat, ordered list — the same top‑to‑bottom flow you see in the funnel builder. Use it to read or visualize how a funnel is laid out.

Each entry in `steps` is one of three kinds:

- **`show_page_step`** — a page. Includes `page` (its `name`, `url`, `external`, `custom_html_page`, and `sdk_token`) and `show_page_step_id` — the id you hand back as `funnel.show_page_step_id` to swap a page onto this step. `external` is true only for a page hosted off ClickFunnels. `custom_html_page` is true when ClickFunnels serves HTML you supplied. `sdk_token` is the token for either of those SDK-powered pages, and null for an editor page.
- **`split_test_step`** — an A/B test: a `variants` list, each with a `weight` and its own `steps`.
- **`conditional_split_step`** — routing by a saved contact filter: a `branches` list, always `[matched, unmatched]`, each with its own `steps`.

Splits can nest — a split placed inside a branch shows up inside that branch's `steps`.

**Two things to know when reading it:**

1. **Follow the array order, not `sort_order`.** `sort_order` only numbers a step within its own list, so it repeats across branches and after splits — in the example below the top level runs `0, 1, 0, 1`. The array order is the real sequence. (Separately: when you *create* a step, the `sort_order` you send positions it among the funnel's top‑level steps.)
2. **Branches come back together.** A branch lists only its own steps; afterwards the flow continues at the step right after the split, and every branch ends up there. In the example below, both branches lead on to `Order Form → Thank You`. A split with nothing after it ends the funnel.

The `200` example below is this funnel:

```text
Entry
└─ Conditional Split
   ├─ matched:     VIP Welcome   → Split Test ( Premium Offer A 50% / Premium Offer B 50% )
   └─ unmatched: Guest Welcome → Conditional Split ( Returning Customer / New Customer )
→ Order Form → Thank You          (every path comes back together here)
```

Related: the [Pages skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/pages/skill.md#positioning-a-page-within-a-funnel) (create, position, and swap pages) and the [Funnels skill](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/funnels/skill.md) (add split tests and conditional splits). When migrating externally-hosted pages to a new domain, this is the read that inventories them: see [Migrate an External Page Domain](https://accounts.myclickfunnels.com/.well-known/sdk/migrate-external-page-domain/skill.md#2-read-and-recursively-inventory-the-funnel).

steps.description: The funnel's visible steps in order (no internal container steps).

items.description:
A step node. Common fields plus type-specific fields keyed off `step_type`:
- `show_page_step`: + `show_page_step_id` + `page` object.
- `conditional_split_step`: + `convergence_step_id` + `branches` array (each branch has a flat `steps` array).
- `split_test_step`: + `convergence_step_id` + `variants` array (each variant has a `weight` and a flat `steps` array).

branches.description: conditional_split_step only. Always `[matched, unmatched]`; each branch carries its own flat `steps` array.

convergence_step_id.description: Split steps only. Id of the step where this split's branches/variants reconverge — the first step that runs after the split, which every path continues to (in the example below all paths rejoin at the Order Form, id 696). null when nothing follows the split. The referenced step always appears in this tree.

custom_html_page.description: True when ClickFunnels serves HTML you supplied. False for editor pages and externally hosted pages.

external.description: True only for a page hosted off ClickFunnels. A custom HTML page is not external.

sdk_token.description: Always present. The SDK token for an external page or a custom HTML page; null for an editor page.

show_page_step_id.description: show_page_step only — the function public id accepted by `funnel.show_page_step_id` on Create/Update Page.

sort_order.description: Position within this step's own container (the top-level sequence, or a single branch/variant) — not globally unique across the flattened list. Walk `steps` in array order to read the visible sequence.

variants.description: split_test_step only. Each variant carries a `weight` and its own flat `steps` array.

post.description:
Abandon an unpaid, draft, or past-due invoice through ClickFunnels' own abandon path (the
same path the in-app "Abandon invoice" button uses) so the abandon propagates to the payment
processor and STOPS its autopay retry (dunning) schedule for this invoice.
